articles.title: Netball Super League to be broadcast on Sky Sports in 2026 with 75 per cent of games shown
articles.summary: Sky Sports will exclusively show the Netball Super Cup, NSL Play-Offs and Grand Final; 75 per cent of all regular Netball Super League matches will also be broadcast live on Sky Sports and Sky Sports YouTube
articles.body:
The league is entering its second year of its journey to professionalisation, building on the success of a 2025 relaunch that delivered record growth in viewing figures.

Ahead of the new season, the Super Cup will return to Sheffield's Utilita Arena on Saturday February 21, marking the first competitive action of the year for all eight clubs and you can watch that match live on Sky Sports Mix from 11.30am.

The Netball Super League regular season then begins on February 27. Throughout this season, Sky Sports will show 75 per cent of the games live on Sky Sports as well as on Sky Sports YouTube.

Helen Falkus, Director of Multi Sports at Sky Sports said: "Netball viewing on Sky Sports doubled last season and we'll be looking to carry that momentum into 2026.

"Seventy-five per cent of matches will again be available live across Sky Sports TV and YouTube channels meaning every fan will continue to have fantastic access.

"As the UK's leading investor in women's sports rights, we're proud to help grow the game and reach new audiences."

Speaking about the announcement, NSL Managing Director Claire Nelson said: "Following last year's landmark broadcast deals, I'm delighted that the Netball Super League will once again make every match available live, giving our fans unrivalled access to the league.

"Ensuring women's sport is accessible to audiences everywhere is crucial to the continued growth of the game, and our broadcast partners, Sky Sports and BBC Sport, play a vital role in that journey.

"Their ongoing support ensures our athletes, our clubs and our competition receive the visibility they deserve. Alongside this, the introduction of new venues and doubleheader matchdays marks another exciting step forward, creating more opportunities for fans to get behind their clubs and engage with the Netball Super League live."

articles.title: Apuestas y pronósticos Valencia vs Villarreal
articles.standfirst: Codere te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta a Valencia y Villarreal en Mestalla correspondiente a la jornada 10 de LaLiga EA Sports 2026-27
articles.summary: Codere te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta a Valencia y Villarreal en Mestalla correspondiente a la jornada 10 de LaLiga EA Sports 2026-27
articles.body: El Valencia afronta una nueva jornada liguera con la urgencia de empezar a sumar de tres en tres. La era de Javier Aguirre ha arrancado con dos empates frente al Racing y al Athletic. Resultados insuficientes para sacar al conjunto che de los puestos de descenso. Mestalla se presenta como una oportunidad para cambiar la dinámica y lograr una victoria que permita al equipo ganar confianza en un momento delicado de la temporada. Favorito para el partido entre Valencia y Villarreal El Villarreal, por su parte, llega después de empatar frente al Elche y con la intención de recuperar la senda del triunfo tras la dolorosa remontada sufrida contra el Liverpool en Champions. El submarino amarillo había encadenado dos victorias ante Málaga y Levante antes del parón de selecciones, por lo que buscará recuperar esa dinámica positiva en una visita exigente. Además, los precedentes recientes favorecen al equipo de La Plana, con tres victorias y dos empates en los últimos cinco enfrentamientos directos. Las casas de apuestas también le conceden el favoritismo: Codere ofrece una cuota de 3.10 por la victoria del Valencia, 3.70 por el empate y 2.15 por el triunfo del Villarreal. Ambos equipos marcan El mercado de ambos equipos marcan ofrece varias tendencias que conviene tener en cuenta en las apuestas deportivas. El Valencia ha cumplido este pronóstico en solamente dos de sus últimos cinco partidos de Liga, mientras que el Villarreal lo ha hecho en tres de sus cinco encuentros más recientes. En los enfrentamientos directos, ambos equipos marcaron en tres de los últimos cinco duelos. Un registro que apunta a una posibilidad real de que los dos conjuntos encuentren portería en Mestalla. Codere ofrece una cuota de 1.62 por el 'sí' y de 2.25 por el 'no'. Número total de goles (Over/Under) Los registros recientes apuntan a un partido con opciones de quedarse por debajo de los 2.5 goles, especialmente si se atiende a los precedentes entre ambos equipos. El Valencia ha superado esa línea en solamente dos de sus últimos cinco encuentros ligueros, mientras que el Villarreal lo ha hecho en tres de sus cinco partidos más recientes. Sin embargo, el dato más significativo aparece en los enfrentamientos directos: únicamente uno de los últimos cinco terminó con más de 2.5 tantos. Una tendencia que invita a valorar un choque más cerrado de lo que sugieren las cuotas. Codere paga a 1.72 que se marquen más de 2.5 goles y a 2.05 que haya menos de 2.5 tantos. Último equipo en marcar El mercado del último equipo en marcar presenta registros idénticos para Valencia y Villarreal en sus últimos cinco partidos: ambos han sido el último conjunto en ver portería en dos ocasiones. Sin embargo, los enfrentamientos directos ofrecen una tendencia más favorable al equipo visitante. El Villarreal marcó el último gol en cuatro de los cinco duelos más recientes contra el Valencia. Un precedente que refuerza su candidatura en este apartado. Codere ofrece una cuota de 1.80 por que el Villarreal marque el último gol, de 2.15 por que lo haga el Valencia y de 9.00 por que el encuentro termine sin goles.

articles.title: Inspiring story on hard work: “You can overcome something, if and only if you love something enough” – How Lionel Messi turned a childhood growth hormone deficiency into eight Ballon d’Or wins
articles.summary: Lionel Messi was ten when doctors in Rosario found that his body wasn't making enough growth hormone.
articles.body: Lionel Messi was ten when doctors in Rosario found that his body wasn't making enough growth hormone. The treatment cost about $900 a month, and his family could not keep up the payments. Barcelona offered to cover the bill, and a boy who barely reached his classmates' shoulders grew up to win eight Ballon d'Or awards, more than any player in history. A line often credited to him explains why he never quit: "You can overcome something, if and only if you love something enough." Here is what it means and how his story backs it up.What Messi meant by "overcome something, if and only if you love something enough"On the surface, the line is simple. Love is the fuel, and obstacles are what it burns through. But the words "if and only if" make it stricter than the usual feel-good advice. Love becomes the one condition that matters. Talent, money and luck can all help, yet without real love for the thing itself, the struggle stops being worth it.Where he said it is harder to pin down. The line has circulated for years on quote websites, and Indian outlets such as Free Press Journal ran it again as a quote of the day on his 39th birthday, 24 June 2026. None of them points to a dated interview or speech, and I could not trace one either. It is best treated as a widely attributed saying, not a verified press-conference moment.That caution matters less than it sounds, because other lines credited to him point the same way. "Everything I did, I did for football, to achieve my dream." And: "You have to fight to reach your dream. You have to sacrifice and work hard for it." Read together, they describe someone who treated football as the point of his life, not a hobby that happened to pay well. His biography gives the words their weight, and it starts in Rosario.How a growth hormone deficiency nearly ended Messi's football dreamMessi was born on 24 June 1987 and picked up a ball almost as soon as he could walk. His father, Jorge, a steelworker, coached a local side, and his grandmother Celia, his first big fan, took him to practice. At Newell's Old Boys, he ran through youth defences. He was also much smaller than everyone else.By ten, his parents knew this was more than a late growth spurt. Doctors diagnosed a growth hormone deficiency. Treatment meant regular injections, and it cost roughly $900 a month. Newell's helped with the bill for a while, then stopped. A steelworker's income and health cover could not carry it alone.Picture what that does to a family. A child with obvious talent, a medical cost they can't meet, and a clock ticking on his growth. River Plate, one of Argentina's biggest clubs, was interested but reportedly would not pay for the treatment either. Football wasn't rejecting Messi. His body, and the price of fixing it, were the real obstacles.The napkin deal and the nightly injections that followedBarcelona saw what Argentina's clubs couldn't. Messi flew to Spain for a trial in September 2000, aged 13, and the club's staff knew quickly they were watching something rare. Sporting director Carles Rexach was reluctant to wait. On 14 December 2000, he wrote an agreement on a paper napkin, and a formal contract followed. Barcelona agreed to pay for the treatment, and the Messi family moved across the Atlantic.The move was not easy. Messi was a shy teenager in a new country, living at the club's La Masia academy while his family struggled to settle. His mother and siblings went back to Rosario for a time. He stayed with his father and kept working.By most accounts, he injected himself in the leg every night for years. Nobody could do it for him, and nobody could play on his behalf. This is the part of the story that makes the quote feel earned. Doing something difficult once is bravery. Doing it every night for years, when you are barely a teenager, is closer to what the quote describes. The treatment worked, and he reached about 5ft 7in, short for an elite striker but enough to compete.From the smallest player on the pitch to eight Ballon d'Or winsMessi made his Barcelona first-team debut in October 2004, aged 17. Many coaches argue his size became an asset, since a low centre of gravity and close control made him very hard to knock off the ball. That is an interpretation, not a medical claim, but his dribbling certainly looked built for tight spaces.The awards followed in bulk. He won the Ballon d'Or in 2009, 2010, 2011, 2012, 2015, 2019, 2021 and 2023. That is eight, a record no other player has reached.The trophies only tell half of it. For years, critics said he had not delivered for Argentina. He lost the 2014 World Cup final and consecutive Copa América finals in 2015 and 2016. After the second, he announced his international retirement, then reversed it. Walking away would have been easier, but he stayed. He won the 2021 Copa América, the 2022 World Cup as captain, and the 2024 Copa América.His eighth Ballon d'Or came in 2023, when he was 36, a long way from a 10-year-old needing a monthly bill paid.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Milwaukee fans pack Deer District for Brewers World Series opener
articles.summary: Milwaukee Brewers fans gathered in the Deer District Oct. 23 to celebrate the team's first World Series appearance in 44 years.
articles.body:
With cheers from fans echoing all the way to Dr. M.L.K. Jr. Drive and Juneau Street in Milwaukee, fans gathered in the Deer District Oct. 23 to watch the Milwaukee Brewers ' return to the World Series after 44 years, following the Milwaukee Bucks' home opener.

The day's celebrations began at 3 p.m. with the Bucks' home opener against the Chicago Bulls . The game was originally scheduled for 7 p.m., but the Bucks moved the tip-off time to 3 p.m. on Oct. 16 to accommodate the Brewers' first World Series appearance since 1982.

Despite the Bucks losing their home opener to the Bulls, 132-125, Bucks fans united with Brewers fans ‒ and even a few Bulls fans ‒ outside Fiserv Forum to watch the Brewers take on the Tampa Bay Rays on a giant screen in the middle of the Deer District.

Photos - Brewers fans pack Deer District for World Series opener

The free outdoor watch party, hosted by Deer District Business Improvement District 53, took place at The Deer Garden.

At least 110 fans gathered around the giant screen, while at least 150 more people opted to watch the game inside the Deer District's bars and restaurants rather than brave the crisp 57-degree weather.

Brewers gear dominated the crowd, with fans sporting jerseys, hats and other team apparel as they gathered to cheer on Milwaukee.

Despite a few technical difficulties with the Jumbotron fading in and out, drawing boos from the crowd, fans continued cheering as they watched a clip of Jacob Misiorowski's now-infamous Pokémon interview , Fox commentators' updated World Series predictions, and Misiorowski stepping up to the mound to throw his historic first pitch , which at 103.5 mph was the fastest-ever pitch thrown in the World Series since pitch tracking began in 2008.

More Brewers World Series watch parties planned in Deer District

The Deer District will continue hosting free outdoor watch parties for the Brewers' upcoming World Series games on Oct. 24, 26 and 27.

Participating bars and restaurants throughout the district offered special promotions during the postseason, including drink specials.

articles.title: Erik Spoelstra is not worried about the Heat's struggles to start the 2026-27 season
articles.summary: The Heat are not off to a great start, even after acquiring Giannis Antetokounmpo.
articles.body:
After the 2026 offseason, the Miami Heat had immense hype surrounding the team. With Giannis Antetokounmpo, anything is possible, but people are down on the Heat right now because of their slow start to the 2026-27 season.

They have lost their first two games of the season to the Minnesota Timberwolves and the Detroit Pistons . Both are formidable opponents, but the second loss in a row does not have head coach Erik Spoelstra worried just yet.

Erik Spoelstra is unbothered by the two losses to start the Heat's season

It has not been the best stretch for the Heat to start the season because a lot of people expected them to at least win one game from the first two. Unfortunately, they were trounced by both opponents.

Now, Spoelstra is back to the drawing board after a nightmare start to the year. As the head coach, he wants to stabilize the team amid all the struggles they are currently facing.

Of course, it is only two games into an 82-game season, so it is not the time to panic. Spoelstra has those sentiments, but he is looking for the best ways to resolve the problems they had during the first two games.

"We're facing a little bit of adversity to start. No one wanted to start 0-2 with our first two home games. I do know this about our locker room: they care... Giannis really cares. He wants this to work; his teammates really want this to work. We're gonna get there," Spoelstra said after the loss to the Pistons .

As long as the players can channel their frustrations into bouncing back, the Heat will be okay. However, they would have preferred to have a win on the board, but at the moment, they will have to motivate themselves.

articles.title: 11-year-old Indian-origin chess prodigy Bodhana Sivanandan breaks legend Judit Polgar's 38-year-old record
articles.summary: Eleven-year-old chess prodigy Bodhana Sivanandan has made history by becoming the youngest female player ever to qualify for the International Master (IM)
articles.body: Eleven-year-old chess prodigy Bodhana Sivanandan has made history by becoming the youngest female player ever to qualify for the International Master (IM) title.The schoolgirl from Harrow, England, achieved the milestone at the European Club Cup in Budva, Montenegro, breaking a record held by chess legend Judit Polgar for 38 years.The English Chess Federation praised Bodhana’s achievement, describing her as an exceptional talent with a bright future in the sport.IM Malcolm Pein, the federation’s Director of International Chess, said, “I can only describe Bodhana as a generational talent. There was no limit to what she can achieve.”Bodhana breaks Judit Polgar’s recordBodhana secured her final required IM norm after facing Sweden’s Woman International Master Viktoria Johansson in the tournament’s last round. At 11 years and seven months, she surpassed Polgar, who achieved the same milestone at 12 in 1988.To qualify for the IM title, players generally need three tournament performances known as norms and a FIDE rating of at least 2400. The title is open to both men and women and ranks just below Grandmaster, the highest title in chess.Pein also praised Bodhana for matching Polgar’s achievements at a similar age, adding, “It’s remarkable that she is more than matching Judit Polgar's achievements at a similar age and breaking her records, even if we live in different times. It's worth noting that Bodhana is the seventh youngest player, boy or girl, to become an International Master.”A remarkable rise in chessBodhana’s latest success follows several major achievements. Last month, she became the youngest player ever to qualify for the Woman Grandmaster title after scoring eight points from 11 games at the Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Uzbekistan.Her progress has been rapid since discovering chess at five during the Covid lockdown. At nine, she became the youngest person selected to represent England internationally in any sport. She later defeated a grandmaster at the 2025 British Chess Championships and beat a player rated above 2600 this July.In August, she also won the British Women’s Chess Championship. Now, with the IM requirements completed before turning 12, Bodhana is moving closer to her next major ambition: becoming a Grandmaster.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: India script history with best-ever fourth-place finish and record 114 medals at Asian Para Games
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India signed off from the Asian Para Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya with a historic performance, securing their best-ever finish of fourth place
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India signed off from the Asian Para Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya with a historic performance, securing their best-ever finish of fourth place and their biggest medal haul across the five editions of the continental event.With the competition concluding on Saturday and only the Closing Ceremony remaining, India finished with a record 114 medals, including 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze. The fourth-place finish also marked a new high for the Indian contingent at the Asian Para Games, underlining the progress made by the country’s para-athletes on the continental stage.India had entered the final day in fourth place, but their position was not confirmed as South Korea remained within striking distance. The Korean contingent needed two more gold medals to draw level with India’s tally of 30, with their superior silver count potentially pushing them ahead.South Korea threaten, but India hold on to fourthSouth Korea added three medals on the final day, taking their overall tally to 100. However, they won only one gold, along with two silver medals, and finished fifth with 29 gold, 38 silver and 33 bronze.That left South Korea one gold short of India, ensuring the Indian contingent retained fourth place. Iran, who finished sixth with 26 gold medals, were also unable to mount a late challenge to India’s position.India’s final tally of 114 medals surpassed their previous best of 108 at the 2022 Asian Para Games in Hangzhou. The 30 gold medals also set a new benchmark for the country at the event.The performance was built on strong contributions across disciplines, with athletics, badminton, archery and shooting among the key medal-winning sports. India’s athletes produced several standout performances and record-breaking efforts during the week-long competition.China dominate as Japan and Uzbekistan complete top threeChina topped the standings by a substantial margin, finishing with 217 gold medals and 435 medals overall. Hosts Japan placed second with 186 medals, including 64 gold, while Uzbekistan took third with 145 medals, including 45 gold.India followed in fourth with 114 medals, ahead of South Korea, Iran, Thailand, Indonesia, Kazakhstan and Saudi Arabia in the top 10.Thailand finished seventh with 125 medals overall, despite having fewer gold medals than the nations above them. Indonesia were eighth, followed by Kazakhstan in ninth and Saudi Arabia in 10th.India’s campaign in Aichi-Nagoya will be remembered for its record medal haul and best-ever finish. The fourth-place result, achieved despite a smaller contingent than the one sent to Hangzhou in 2022, gives the country a new benchmark to build on at the next edition of the Asian Para Games.The final top 10 medal standings reflect China’s dominance and the strong performances of Japan and Uzbekistan, while India’s fourth-place finish represents a historic milestone for the country’s para-sport movement.Asian Para Games 2026: Top 10 nations in the final medal tallyRankNationsGoldSilverBronzeTotal1China2071171114352Japan6460621863Uzbekistan4549511454INDIA3035491145South Korea2938331006Iran2636401027Thailand1940661258Indonesia152137739Kazakhstan1216225010Saudi Arabia88117Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Ronaldinho’s comeback with Ravenna at 46 set for next month at Forli
articles.summary: Ex-Barcelona forward to make November return, having last played for Brazilian club Fluminense in 2015.
articles.body:
Brazil great Ronaldinho will return to competitive football next month when he plays for Italian third-tier side Ravenna against local rivals Forli on November 15, the Serie C club has announced.

The 46-year-old former Barcelona and AC Milan forward, who won the 2002 World Cup with Brazil and the Ballon d’Or in 2005, last played competitively for Brazilian club Fluminense in 2015. He officially retired in 2018.

Ravenna signed Ronaldinho in June and announced his return to the pitch on Friday. Ronaldinho acquired a stake in the club, which is owned by his friend Ignazio Cipriani.

Cipriani said the move was intended “to bring the whole city closer to the team”.

Ronaldinho stopped short of confirming he would play when he arrived in Italy in August although he left open the prospect of scoring the 300th goal of his career. He currently has 299.

“I’m here to help,” he said at the time.

The derby against Forli will take place at Ravenna’s Stadio Bruno Benelli. Ravenna sit second in Serie C Group B with 20 points from 10 games, eight behind leaders Spezia.

articles.title: Compra este Ferrari F50 por 380.000 euros en 1997, no lo estrena y ahora confía en venderlo por más de 17 millones
articles.standfirst: El coche ha multiplicado su cotización por 45 dando la razón a su propietario, quien renunció a disfrutarlo para venderlo con los años por una auténtica fortuna
articles.summary: El coche ha multiplicado su valor por 45 dando la razón a su propietario, quien renunció a disfrutarlo para venderlo con los años por una auténtica fortuna
articles.body: La historia de este Ferrari F50 que ves en las fotos no está salpicada de momentos emocionantes vividos al volante por parte de su propietario. De hecho, este lo compró en 1997 y se puede decir que casi ni lo ha disfrutado, como demuestra el hecho de que solo tenga 106 millas en su marcador (171 kilómetros). Y eso contando con que el concesionario siempre te lo entrega ya con algunos kilómetros en su marcador. Sin duda, estamos ante un coleccionista que quería conservarlo sabiendo que se trataba de uno de los Ferrari más especiales. Seguro que también tenía presente que si lo guardaba sin usar, su revalorización en el futuro sería estratosférica. Y ahora ha llegado el momento de que presuma de no haberse equivocado, porque el coche será una de las estrellas de la subasta que Broad Arrow Auctions celebrará el 31 de octubre en el hotel Wynn de Las Vegas y la casa de subastas espera venderlo por más de 20 millones de dólares, lo que equivale a superar los 17 millones de euros. Para entender semejante valoración hay que recordar qué es un Ferrari F50. Presentado en el Salón de Ginebra de 1995, este súper deportivo llegó para celebrar el 50 aniversario de la marca italiana y tomar el relevo del mítico F40. Su planteamiento era acercar la experiencia de un Fórmula 1 a un coche de carretera, con una mecánica atmosférica de doce cilindros, cambio manual y una carrocería biplaza de tipo targa, con techo desmontable. El motor era un V12 de 4,7 litros derivado del propulsor que Ferrari había utilizado en su monoplaza de Fórmula 1 de 1990, el 641. Eso sí, no se trataba simplemente de instalar sin más un motor de carreras: hubo que adaptarlo para su uso en carretera, donde, con 520 CV y sin turbo, entregaba la potencia de una forma muy diferente a la de los motores sobrealimentados que aún tenían protagonismo en aquellos años. Las prestaciones siguen siendo a día de hoy espectaculares: alcanzaba los 325 km/h y aceleraba de 0 a 100 km/h en 3,7 segundos. La potencia llegaba a las ruedas traseras a través de una caja de cambios manual de seis velocidades, con la clásica rejilla metálica que permitía guiar sin error la palanca. Una receta que, por mucho que avance la tecnología, sigue teniendo un atractivo especial para quienes buscan una conducción sin los actuales filtros electrónicos. Ferrari fabricó solo 349 unidades del F50 entre 1995 y 1997, una menos de las 350 que inicialmente se habían previsto. El ejemplar que ahora sale a subasta lleva el número de chasis 107165 y es el número 334 de esa reducida serie. Fue entregado nuevo por Maranello Sales, un concesionario situado en Egham, en el condado inglés de Surrey, y es uno de los aproximadamente 25 F50 que llegaron nuevos al Reino Unido. La carrocería luce el característico Rosso Corsa y el interior es de cuero negro con inserciones rojas en los asientos. Conserva además el techo rígido desmontable, que permite transformar su configuración, además de un buen número de accesorios de fábrica como el juego de maletas Schedoni, herramientas, fundas para el coche y los asientos e incluso unos botines para conducirlo en los que pone F50 y que, por supuesto, no han sido estrenados. Pero, por encima de todo, lo que convierte a este F50 en una pieza tan especial es su bajísimo kilometraje. Broad Arrow asegura que probablemente sea el ejemplar con menos kilómetros. La pregunta es si alguien estará dispuesto a pagar más de 17 millones de euros por un coche que hace tres décadas costaba unos 390.000 euros. Pero en Broad Arrow no hablan por hablar ni equivocan tanto el tiro, así que es muy posible que se alcance y supere esta cifra.

articles.body: Asian Para Games Closing Ceremony: 4,000 athletes from 45 countries and regions The closing ceremony of the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games was held at the Mizuho Park Athletics Stadium in Nagoya on Saturday, bringing the week-long competition to an end. Held in Japan for the first time, the Games brought together approximately 4,000 athletes and staff from 45 countries and regions. The Asian Para Games evolved from the Far East and South Pacific Games Federation for the Disabled, with the inaugural edition held in Guangzhou, China, in 2010. The Aichi-Nagoya event marked the fifth edition, with Doha set to host the sixth in 2030..Asian Para Games Closing Ceremony: 4,000 athletes from 45 countries and regioms The closing ceremony of the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games was held at the Mizuho Park Athletics Stadium in Nagoya on Saturday, bringing the week-long competition to an end. Held in Japan for the first time, the Games brought together approximately 4,000 athletes and staff from 45 countries and regions. The Asian Para Games evolved from the Far East and South Pacific Games Federation for the Disabled, with the inaugural edition held in Guangzhou, China, in 2010. The Aichi-Nagoya event marked the fifth edition, with Doha set to host the sixth in 2030..That was absolutely fantastic! .Asian Para Games Closing Ceremony: India’s para-swimmers make significant progress India finished the Asian Para Games swimming competition with 11 medals, comprising three silver and eight bronze, a significant improvement on the solitary bronze secured at the previous edition. Budigina won silver in the men’s S13 100m backstroke and freestyle events before adding bronze in the 50m freestyle. Nandal’s journey to the continental podium has been marked by determination and a willingness to embrace new challenges. Hailing from a sports-oriented family in Rohtak, Haryana, he moved to Delhi at the age of four and joined the National Association for the Blind, where he learnt Braille. He initially pursued judo and won medals at the national level before switching to swimming in 2021. His progress culminated in becoming the first Indian blind swimmer to achieve the Minimum Qualification Standard for the Paris Paralympics in 2024. His three-bronze performance in Aichi-Nagoya marked another milestone in his sporting journey..Asian Para Games Closing Ceremony: ‘The finish came down to mere microseconds’ Nandal had earlier secured bronze in the men’s 400m freestyle and 100m breaststroke S11 events, completing a memorable campaign with three podium finishes. He opened his medal account on Tuesday in the 400m freestyle with a time of 5:10.91 before adding another bronze in the breaststroke. Recalling the intensity of the latter race, Nandal said the outcome was decided by the narrowest of margins. “The 100-metre breaststroke was the most challenging. The race was so intense that the finish came down to mere microseconds. If I had been even a fraction further behind—by a distance no greater than the thickness of a strand of hair—I would have lost the medal,” he said. The S11 classification is for swimmers with severe visual impairment, including those with very low visual acuity or no light perception. Nandal’s three medals made him one of India’s standout performers in the pool, alongside Ravi Budigina, who also won three medals..Asian Para Games Closing Ceremony: Himanshu Nandal dedicates historic medal treble to nation Indian para-swimmer Himanshu Nandal dedicated his historic hat-trick of bronze medals at the Asian Para Games 2026 to the nation and his support staff, crediting their hard work and dedication for his achievements in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan. The 22-year-old completed his treble on Friday by finishing third in the men’s 100m freestyle S11 event, helping India end its campaign with 11 medals in the pool. “It feels wonderful. I also achieved personal bests, and I managed to secure three bronze medals. I would like to dedicate this achievement to the nation and to my support staff, who worked so hard and with such dedication to make this possible,” Nandal told ANI. Born blind due to optic nerve failure, Nandal clocked one minute and 5.90 seconds in the 100m freestyle. .Asian Para Games Closing Ceremony: The ceremony begins in Nagoya The Asian Para Games 2026 is drawing to a close today, with a grand closing ceremony at the Nagoya City Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium in Nagoya, Japan. Celebrations to bid farewell to the athletes and mark the end of a memorable edition are now underway..Asian Para Games Closing Ceremony: Final prep going on in Nagoya stadium .Asian Para Games Closing Ceremony: The grand ceremony will start soon .Asian Para Games Closing Ceremony: When & where to watch the ceremony When >> The Asian Para Games 2026 closing ceremony will take place on Saturday, October 24, at the Nagoya City Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium in Nagoya, Aichi Prefecture, Japan. The ceremony is scheduled to begin at 2:30 PM IST (6 PM local time). Where to watch >> The closing ceremony will be telecast live on DD Sports in India. Viewers can also watch the live stream on the Prasar Bharati Sports YouTube channel and the WAVES OTT platform..Asian Para Games Closing Ceremony: JLN-trained athletes deliver strong medal haul The group produced an impressive showing across track and field events in Aichi-Nagoya. Praveen Kumar won gold in the men’s high jump T64, while Sandeep Kumar claimed the men’s 400m T64 title with a world-record performance. Pranav Soorma triumphed in the men’s club throw F51, and Rinku Hooda won the men’s javelin F46 event. Simran Sharma completed a sprint double, winning gold in the women’s 100m and 200m T12 and setting Games records in both races. Silver medallists from the training group included Manjeet in the men’s javelin F12/F13, Nimisha Chakkungalparambil in the women’s long jump T47, Varun Singh Bhati in the men’s high jump T63, Preeti Pal in the women’s 100m and 200m T35, and Ajeet Singh Yadav in the men’s javelin F46. Sandeep Kumar also won bronze in the men’s 100m T44, while Sandip Sanjay Sargar secured bronze in the men’s javelin combined-classification event. Anubhav Choudhary finished third in the men’s 100m T35, alongside Navdeep’s bronze. Their performances highlighted the contribution of the JLN Stadium’s training environment to India’s record-breaking campaign..Asian Para Games Closing Ceremony: Dedicated training space helps athletes focus Navdeep also highlighted the benefits of having access to the stadium’s main track and dedicated training areas, saying the facility helped athletes prepare without unnecessary interruptions or delays. He explained that training at the JLN Stadium allowed him to concentrate on his throws rather than waiting for other athletes to finish their turns. “Sprinters need an empty track, so they got a good chance to train inside it. I majorly train at the SAI Regional Centres (Bengaluru, Sonipat and Gandhinagar), where there is not much crowd and I don’t have to wait for other athletes to finish their throws. This all happened here at the JLN Stadium too. I could focus on my preparations rather than focusing on rotations and waiting for my turn,” Navdeep said. He also expressed hope of returning to the facility next season. More than 50 other para-athletes train at the SAI JLN Stadium, which continues to serve as a base for athletes across disciplines. Navdeep was among 14 medallists at the Asian Para Games who trained there ahead of the continental competition..Asian Para Games Closing Ceremony: JLN Stadium support helps Navdeep prepare for Asian Para Games Indian para-athlete Navdeep Singh has credited the training environment and support at the Sports Authority of India’s Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium in New Delhi for helping him prepare for the Asian Para Games 2026, where he won bronze in the men’s javelin throw F40/F41 event. Navdeep, a Paris Paralympics gold medallist, improved on his fourth-place finish at the 2022 Asian Para Games by securing a podium finish in Aichi-Nagoya. “Most of us Asian Games-bound athletes, including me, did our preparations at the JLN Stadium for the Asian Games 2026,” Navdeep said after his medal-winning performance. “This allowed us to acclimatise and get the feel. Despite the ongoing (Indian Super League) football matches, they kept the Asian Games a priority, which I felt was quite impressive, and that supported me,” he added..Asian Para Games Closing Ceremony: "IMAGINE ONE HEART: Hearts as one" .Asian Para Games Closing Ceremony: India's best-ever finish!!! .Asian Para Games Closing Ceremony: India script history with best-ever fourth-place finish India signed off from the Asian Para Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya with a historic performance, securing their best-ever finish of fourth place and their biggest medal haul across the five editions of the continental event. With the competition concluding on Saturday and only the Closing Ceremony remaining, India finished with a record 114 medals, including 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze. The fourth-place finish also marked a new high for the Indian contingent at the Asian Para Games, underlining the progress made by the country’s para-athletes on the continental stage. India had entered the final day in fourth place, but their position was not confirmed as South Korea remained within striking distance. The Korean contingent needed two more gold medals to draw level with India’s tally of 30, with their superior silver count potentially pushing them ahead..Asian Para Games Closing Ceremony: Meet India's flag-bearers at closing ceremony Double gold medallists Mona Agarwal and Nishad Kumar will be India's flag-bearers at the closing ceremony of the 2026 Asian Para Games in Aichi-Nagoya on Saturday, following outstanding campaigns in shooting and para-athletics. Both athletes won two gold medals each at the continental event, with Mona producing a record-breaking performance in shooting and Nishad excelling in the high jump and long jump. Their selection as flag-bearers recognises their achievements as India prepare to bring the Games to a close..Asian Para Games Closing Ceremony: India record historic medal haul India also completed a landmark campaign, finishing with a record 114 medals — 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze. The tally surpassed the country’s previous best of 108 medals at the 2022 edition in Hangzhou. India’s 168-member para-athlete contingent delivered world-record performances, historic victories and podium sweeps across multiple disciplines, despite being significantly smaller than the 309 athletes who represented the country in Hangzhou..Asian Para Games Closing Ceremony: Japan set for second-place finish Japan won 186 medals, including 64 gold, 60 silver and 62 bronze, to stand second in the final medal standings behind China. Takaichi expressed hope that Team Japan would build on its performances at the Los Angeles 2028 Paralympic Games and the next Asian Para Games in Doha, Qatar, in 2030..Asian Para Games Closing Ceremony: Gratitude to athletes and support teams Takaichi expressed gratitude to the athletes for inspiring people across Japan, while paying tribute to their families, coaches and others who had supported their journeys. She said the Games provided an opportunity to showcase the appeal of para sports to audiences in Japan and abroad, helping more people connect with the disciplines..Asian Para Games Closing Ceremony: Japanese PM on Asian Para Games .Asian Para Games Closing Ceremony: ‘Profound beauty’ of para sports In a post on X, Takaichi said the athletes had embraced the possibility of failure, believed in themselves and pushed their limits on the big stage. She also praised competitors for supporting teammates, persevering in pursuit of victory and applauding their rivals’ efforts..Asian Para Games Closing Ceremony: Japan hosts Asian Para Games for first time The Games began on October 18 and concluded on October 24 in Aichi-Nagoya, marking the first time Japan hosted the continental para-sports event. Takaichi lauded Team Japan’s performances across disciplines, highlighting the athletes’ teamwork, determination and sportsmanship..Asian Para Games Closing Ceremony: Takaichi praises athletes’ spirit Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi today praised the determination and achievements of athletes at the Asian Para Games 2026, saying their performances showcased the “profound beauty” of para sports as the Aichi-Nagoya Games drew to a close..Asian Para Games Closing Ceremony: India sign off with record medal haul Hello and welcome to the live coverage of the closing ceremony of the Asian Para Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan. India signed off with a historic campaign, securing their best-ever fourth-place finish in the final medal standings. The Indian contingent clinched a record 114 medals, comprising 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze, surpassing its previous best of 108 medals at the 2022 edition in Hangzhou. As the Games draw to a close, India’s para-athletes have set a new benchmark with a memorable campaign featuring record-breaking performances and historic achievements.

articles.title: Chicago Bulls storm back from early deficit to beat Milwaukee Bucks in NBA
articles.summary: Jayson Tatum puts up 36 as Boston Celtics send NY Knicks to second straight loss and Lakers surge past Clippers.
articles.body:
Norman Powell has scored 25 points, and rookie Caleb Wilson has added 21 to help the visiting Chicago Bulls earn a 132-125 victory over the Milwaukee Bucks.

Leonard Miller had 19 points on Friday while Jalen Smith chipped in 14 points and 13 rebounds for Chicago, who rebounded after suffering a 43-point loss to the Toronto Raptors on Wednesday.

Buddy Hield scored 13, Isaac Okoro had 12 and Tre Jones tallied 11 points and eight assists for the Bulls, who trailed by 15 points after the first quarter.

Tyler Herro led Milwaukee with 34 points, followed by Jaime Jaquez Jr’s 19 points and 11 boards. Kyle Kuzma scored 14, and Myles Turner had 12 while Ryan Rollins, AJ Green and Kel’el Ware scored 11 apiece for the Bucks, who lost their second straight game to open the season.

Rookie Brayden Burries made a three-pointer, and Ware scored around the rim to give the Bucks a five-point lead with 2:55 left in the third quarter. Smith beat the third-quarter buzzer with a dunk that cut the Bulls’ deficit to 104-102 entering the fourth.

Chicago scored the first six points of the final quarter and grabbed a 108-104 lead on Wilson’s slam. The Bulls pushed the lead to eight on Hield’s trey with 7:19 remaining.

With Milwaukee trailing by five, Herro connected on back-to-back three-pointers, returning the lead to the Bucks.

Wilson made two free throws to put the Bulls ahead 124-123 with 1:16 left.

After Jones picked off Rollins’s pass, Wilson made another pair from the foul line to push the lead to three. A missed three-pointer by Herro and two more free throws from Powell gave the Bulls a five-point cushion with 20 seconds left.

Wilson’s steal and Jones’s subsequent two foul shots sealed Chicago’s victory.

Milwaukee jumped out to a 19-6 lead on Herro’s first triple less than five minutes in. Green sank a three-pointer in the closing seconds of the first quarter to give the Bucks a 32-17 advantage.

Matas Buzelis’s slam pulled the Bulls within seven, but Kasparas Jakucionis and Rollins hit consecutive treys to build the margin to 44-31 with 8:35 left in the first half.

Chicago answered again and took a 55-51 lead on Hield’s three-pointer, which stamped a 16-0 run.

Kuzma made a layup with three seconds left in the first half to give the Bucks a 62-61 halftime edge.

Hawks crush Hornets, set franchise mark for largest win

Jalen Johnson and reserve Aaron Wiggins each scored 19 points as visiting Atlanta blew out the Charlotte Hornets 128-81, the ‌biggest margin of victory in Hawks history.

The 47-point gap topped the old record of 46 set in a 126-80 victory over the Sacramento Kings in 2017. Nickeil Alexander-Walker put up 14 points, CJ McCollum posted 13 points, Dyson Daniels contributed 11 points, nine rebounds and ⁠seven steals and Corey Kispert also had 11 points for Atlanta, which ⁠won its second straight to start the season.

It was a miserable home opener for the Hornets, who won two nights earlier at Brooklyn to start their campaign. They committed 27 turnovers. Naz Reid scored 17 points for Charlotte and Grayson Allen came off the bench for 11 points. Both players were in their home debuts with the Hornets. Reserve Tidjane Salaun also scored 11 points.

The gap reached 97-62 by the end of the third quarter. The Hornets couldn’t even get it cranked ⁠up when the margin was out of hand, needing about six and a half minutes to reach a double-digit total in the fourth quarter.

Celtics send Knicks to second straight loss

Jayson Tatum scored a game-high 36 points, including nine late in the fourth quarter, as the Boston Celtics withstood a late comeback bid by the visiting New York Knicks to escape with a 107-103 victory.

Tatum finished with nine rebounds and seven assists for the Celtics, who have split their first two games. Paul George and reserve Neemias Queta had 15 points apiece while Derrick White added 12 points.

Celtics centre Mitchell Robinson, the lone member of the Knicks’ rotation who didn’t return to the defending NBA champions, had four points and four rebounds in 22-plus minutes.

Karl-Anthony Towns (22 points, 10 rebounds), OG Anunoby (20 points, 10 rebounds) and Josh Hart (10 points, 12 rebounds) all had double-doubles for the Knicks, who have lost their first two games.

New York has taken consecutive losses for the first time since dropping Games 2 and 3 of an Eastern Conference first-round playoff series against the Atlanta Hawks in April, after which the Knicks won 15 of the next 16 games to clinch their first title since 1973.

Miles McBride scored 20 points off the New York bench while Jalen Brunson had 19 points.

The Celtics led by as many as 12 points three times in the fourth quarter, the last at 94-82 on a three-point play by Queta, before the Knicks mounted a 9-0 run. Boston missed seven consecutive shots as New York rallied.

Towns dunked to pull the Knicks within 94-91 with 4:09 left, but he missed a long three-point attempt 28 seconds later, and Tatum responded with a layup to end the Celtics’ drought.

The Knicks got within 99-98 on Brunson’s fallaway jumper with 1:41 remaining, but Tatum sank a turnaround over Hart after a timeout, and Towns was whistled for an illegal screen on the next possession. Tatum then hit a long corner fallaway, again over Hart, to extend the lead to 103-98.

Anunoby answered with two free throws, but Tatum hit a three-pointer on the next possession. McBride sank a three-pointer before Payton Pritchard iced the win by splitting a pair of free throws with 11 seconds left.

Lakers ride 39-point third quarter to surge past Clippers

Austin Reaves scored 28 points and added nine assists while Luka Doncic recorded 23 points as the Los Angeles Lakers used a third-quarter surge to stay perfect through two games with a 125-117 victory over the visiting Los Angeles Clippers.

Walker Kessler scored 22 points, Ziaire Williams contributed 14 and Matisse Thybulle and Quentin Grimes each had 13 as the Lakers won for the ninth time in their past 13 games against the cross-town Clippers.

Kessler hit 10 of 14 shots from the floor and is now 22 of 26 over two games with his new team after a trade from the Utah Jazz in July. The Lakers had 13 steals and forced the Clippers into 26 turnovers, which they turned into 33 points.

Doncic committed 11 turnovers while Kessler and Grimes led all rebounders with eight apiece.

Darius Garland scored 26 points, and Brook Lopez added 22 as the Clippers dropped their first road game of the season. Derrick Jones Jr and Rui Hachimura each scored 16 points.

The Clippers shot 49.4 percent from the floor and 43.2 percent from three-point range but lost as the Lakers shot 58.2 percent from the floor and 43.8 percent from distance.

The Lakers led 77-76 with 7:18 remaining in the third quarter when a three-pointer from Thybulle kicked off a 14-1 run that gave them a 91-77 lead with 3:43 remaining in the period.

The Lakers took a 103-90 lead into the fourth quarter after scoring 39 points in the third while shooting 72.7 percent from the floor.

The Clippers used an 8-0 run to pull within 119-113 on a three-pointer from Garland with 3:21 to play before Grimes sealed the victory on two free throws with 40.9 seconds remaining for a 125-117 lead.

The Clippers led 31-27 after one quarter and went up by as many as 11 points less than three minutes into the second before the Lakers closed the gap. A three-point play by Doncic with 5.6 seconds remaining tied the game 64-64 at the half.

Doncic led all scorers with 16 points before the break.

articles.title: España gana tres de las cuatro finales ante Euskadi en el Mundial
articles.standfirst: La penúltima jornada dejó cuatro duelos entre españoles y vascos. Los primeros ganaron en mano individual, cesta punta y paleta goma femenina. Los segundos, en mano parejas
articles.summary: La penúltima jornada dejó cuatro duelos entre españoles y vascos. Los primeros ganaron en mano individual, cesta punta y paleta goma femenina. Los segundos, en mano parejas
articles.body: España, 3; Euskadi, 1. Así se puede resumir lo sucedido en las cuatro finales que enfrentaron a pelotaris de la delegación española con los de la vasca, en la penúltima jornada del Mundial de Pelota, que se celebra en Buenos Aires. La inclusión de la Federación Vasca como miembro de pleno derecho en la Federación Internacional a finales de 2024 ha llevado a que por primera vez se vean partidos entre pelotaris de un mismo país en un campeonato del Mundo. España se impuso a Euskadi en las finales de mano individual, cesta punta individual femenina y paleta goma femenina. El combinado vasco se llevó el oro en mano parejas. En mano individual, Jorge Fernández no dio opción a Ekmi Irribarria ni luego a Gaizka Carregal cuando el seleccionador vasco apostó por cambiar a su pelotari en el segundo set. El primero se lo llevó el riojano por un contundente 10-0. El segundo lo cerró con un 10-4. "Salí muy serio sabiendo que estos partidos se deciden por detalles. Jugando con actitud, me ha salido todo de cara", comentó Jorge Fernández al acabar el encuentro. En la cesta punta femenina, Erika Mugartegui se anotó la victoria ante Hele Barrenetxea en un partido de lo más igualado. La española se llevó el primer set por 15-11. En el segundo, Barrenetxea llegó a estar 14-13 arriba para forzar el tercero, pero Mugartegui firmó dos puntos seguidos para dar el oro a España. En paleta goma, Maider Ardanaz se impuso a Nagor Martín por 15-10 y 15-13. La jugadora vasca alargó el partido tras pasar en el segundo set de un 13-6 en contra a un 14-13, pero finalmente no pudo culminar su remontada. Ardanaz se desquitó así de la derrota que había sufrido ante Martín en la primera fase. "Sabía que tenía que empezar a tope, llevar la iniciativa desde el principio. Me ha salido casi todo, al final se me fue un poco, pero pude controlarlo", comentó Ardanaz. La única final entre España y Euskadi que cayó del lado de los vascos fue la de mano parejas. Oier Elorz y Eñaut Lizeaga se impusieron a Oian Canabal y Unax Apeztegia por 10-7 y 10-9. La dupla española llegó a tener dos pelotas para ir al tercer set, pero Elorz las neutralizó y dio el oro a Euskadi. Con anterioridad, España ya había ganado a Euskadi en la final de cesta punta femenina en frontón de 54 metros, en la que Erika Mugartegui y Arai Lejardi vencieron a Maite Ortiz de Mendívil y Maia Goikoetxea. España se colgó dos oros más en los partidos que habían quedado suspendidos la jornada anterior porque la humedad había convertido la pista en un suelo resbaladizo. Luis Sánchez e Íker Espinal se llevaron el oro ante los franceses Peio Larralde y Andoni Iphar en mano parejas en trinquete al ganar por 15-7 y 15-6. El otro título mundial llegó en xare. Joxi Lopetegui, cuyo hijo juega con Euskadi, y Sebastián Moncada ganaron a los franceses Bruno Driolet y Andoni Castera por 15-7 y 15-6. La delegación española además se colgó la plata por partida doble en frontenis al caer en las finales de parejas ante México: Víctor Molina y Gustavo Vidal perdieron ante Isaac Pérez y Jorge Olivera (15-3 y 15-8) y Elena Agulló y Lidia Simón ante Guadalupe Hernández y Ximena Placito (15-14 y 15-13). En la final masculina individual, Gustavo Vidal también se tuvo que conformar con el segundo puesto del podio tras perder ante el argentino Federico Fernández por 13-15, 15-6 y 10-9. En paleta cuero llegó la cuarta plata para España. Miki Fernández de Lascoiti e Iñigo Ansó perdieron ante los argentinos Federico Andreassen y Alfredo Villegas por 15-9 y 15-6. Además, en cesta punta masculina España logró el bronce. Rubén Bailo venció al mexicano Marco Antonio Ochoa por 15-10 y 15-7. Aritz Erkiaga se colgó el oro en la final de la cesta punta masculina tras ganar al francés Olharan por 15-12 y 15-7. En su debut mundialista, Euskadi suma ya cuatro oros (cesta punta parejas masculina, parapelota en trinquete, mano parejas y cesta punta individual masculina) y cuatro platas (en cesta punta parejas femenina, mano individual, cesta punta individual femenina y paleta goma femenina). Este sábado se cierra el Mundial y habrá otra final entre España y Euskadi. Será en la pala corta.

articles.title: Trump calls for WNBA boycott over anthem walkouts, warning teams ‘they will destroy themselves’
articles.summary: President Trump calls for a boycott of the WNBA after players from the Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries walk out during the national anthem, igniting a political debate as the Finals continue.
articles.body: The WNBA’s Finals have drawn attention for their basketball, but the pregame routine of two teams has become a political flashpoint. Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries players have left the court before the national anthem in each of the first three games of their best-of-seven series, prompting criticism from President Donald Trump, Vice President JD Vance and some fans. With Game 4 approaching, the league has yet to publicly address the controversy.Trump urges fans to boycott women’s basketballTrump addressed the walkouts during a rally in Iowa on Thursday, October 1, while campaigning for Republican candidates ahead of the midterm elections. He compared the WNBA players’ actions with NFL protests a decade earlier, when some players knelt during the national anthem to protest police brutality.“By the way, what’s going on with the women’s NBA? What’s that all about? They’ll destroy themselves before they get started because they just started to do good…,” Trump said, according to a video shared on X by conservative influencer Nick Sortor.The president then questioned why players were leaving the court while the anthem played and urged people to stop watching women’s basketball unless the teams changed their routine.“It’s a big deal going on. They leave the court when the national anthem’s playing. What’s that all about?” Trump said. “The NFL did that for a while and they stopped because people stopped watching the games. So I think you should do the same thing with women’s basketball.”He repeated the comparison and called for a boycott unless players remained on the court during the anthem.The criticism followed comments from Vice President JD Vance, who described the players’ conduct as “disgraceful” during an interview with Raymond Arroyo. Vance said the players “have a lot to be grateful to the United States for, and I think that if they had a bit more of a spirit of gratitude, they'd be happier people, and they wouldn't offend so many people as well.”Why the teams are leaving the courtThe walkouts have occurred before all three games of the Finals, with the Valkyries holding a 2-1 series lead. OutKick reporter Dan Zaksheske shared videos of the teams’ departures and contacted the league, Atlanta and Golden State for an explanation, but received no response.Zaksheske described the scene before Game 1: “Both teams were on the floor beforehand, warming up for the game, then disappeared for roughly the two minutes it took to perform the ‘Star-Spangled Banner.’”Speaking to reporters before Game 2, Golden State guard Veronica Burton said the absence from the court was part of the team’s established routine, rather than a new political statement.“We’ve been doing that. That’s just our pregame routine. We’ve been doing that since last year,” Burton said, responding to a reporter’s assumption that the walkout was political.Atlanta last addressed its anthem position publicly in 2020, when the Dream said the anthem “does not represent freedom, justice, and liberty for all Americans.” The teams have not commented publicly on the current controversy, and the WNBA has also remained silent.What the WNBA rules say, and what happens nextThe league’s rulebook says players, coaches and trainers “are to stand and line up in a dignified posture along the sidelines or on the foul line during the playing of the National Anthem.” The wording does not clearly establish whether the requirement applies to everyone on a team or only those already on the court.The WNBA suspended enforcement of its anthem protocols in 2017, after players and coaches sought to show solidarity with victims of violence in Charlottesville, Virginia, following a white nationalist rally. The Associated Press reported that the league’s protocols had been suspended, despite the rulebook’s language.Teams also left the court before the anthem during the 2020 season, which the WNBA dedicated to Breonna Taylor, who was killed in her Louisville, Kentucky, home. Atlanta’s game notes that August included messaging from the players’ union explaining anthem protests. Many teams have continued to leave the court before the anthem in subsequent seasons, often as part of their pregame routine or in connection with social justice issues.The controversy now follows the Finals into Game 4, scheduled for October 24, 2026, at State Farm Arena. The Valkyries lead the series 2-1, while the teams, league and fans await any further response to Trump’s call for a boycott.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Asesinan a tiros al presidente de la Federación Búlgara de Taekwondo
articles.standfirst: El móvil del crimen, ocurrido el día de reflexión previo a las elecciones presidenciales, fue una "disputa doméstica", según el Ministerio del Interior
articles.summary: El móvil del crimen, ocurrido el día de reflexión previo a las elecciones presidenciales, fue una "disputa doméstica", según el Ministerio del Interior
articles.body: El presidente de la Federación Búlgara de Taekwondo, Slavcho Binev, antiguo eurodiputado, miembro del Parlamento búlgaro, excampeón y figura destacada de las artes marciales en el país balcánico, además de controvertido empresario, fue asesinado a tiros este sábado en su domicilio, situado en un barrio exclusivo de Sofía. Fuentes del Ministerio del Interior confirmaron a EFE el suceso, aunque se limitaron a explicar que el móvil del crimen, ocurrido el sábado, día de reflexión previo a las elecciones presidenciales, fue una "disputa doméstica".Añadieron que los presuntos autores, tres hombres armados, fueron detenidos en una autopista cuando intentaban huir de Sofía. Conocido como 'Slavi' Binev, de 60 años, fue competidor de taekwondo y campeón europeo en 1992, además de ser luego político y propietario de numerosos locales nocturnos de Sofía. Durante años también entrenó a la selección nacional de este deporte, antes de ocupar puestos directivos en distintas organizaciones deportivas, entre ellas la Federación Búlgara de Taekwondo, cuya presidencia renovó por un mandato de cinco años en mayo pasado. Además, ha sido durante años miembro de la junta ejecutiva del Comité Olímpico Búlgaro. Inició su carrera política en el partido ultranacionalista y de extrema derecha Ataka, en cuyas listas fue elegido miembro del Parlamento Europeo en 2007. Volvió a obtener un escaño como eurodiputado tras las elecciones europeas celebradas en Bulgaria en 2009. Entró en el Parlamento búlgaro tras las elecciones legislativas de 2014, esta vez como miembro del Frente Patriótico, otra formación nacionalista. Su nombre está estrechamente ligado a los años convulsos de la década de 1990, durante la transición del régimen comunista a la democracia, una época marcada por el crimen organizado y las guerras entre bandas criminales

articles.title: "Just undriveable" – Isack Hadjar looking for answers after "massive" struggles in Austin practice
articles.summary: While Verstappen spoke of a largely positive start in Austin, Hadjar concluded that he had gone in the wrong direction with his set-up. His front tyres were...
articles.body:
It was a day of contrasting fortunes for Red Bull during Formula 1 practice at the Circuit of the Americas. Max Verstappen was largely satisfied with the early signs of the RB22, although he stressed that the balance between high-speed and low-speed corners still needed improvement, with technical director Pierre Wache indicating that Red Bull needed to make gains in the slower sections of the track.

Verstappen used the word 'fine-tuning', but things are certainly not at that stage on the other side of the garage. Isack Hadjar had a largely positive feeling during FP1, despite finishing 14th in the standings, but decided to explore a slightly different set-up direction for the second session of the day.

"I did [make a lot of changes after FP1]. I was happy-ish with how it went this morning. Afterwards, I thought I was heading in the right direction, but it only brought a lot more problems", the Frenchman concluded.

"I still felt okay on the medium, even though we changed the car. But on the soft, the car was completely gone for me. It was very difficult to drive, so I need to turn things around tomorrow.

"We need to sit down and see what we can do because the car made a massive step down. We need to bring it back, at least to the level it was this morning."

Hadjar had already been voicing his frustrations over the team radio during FP2. His qualifying simulation in particular fell apart, leaving him almost a full second behind team-mate Verstappen at the end of the day.

The balance problems caused Hadjar's front tyres to overheat extremely quickly, with all the consequences that entailed.

"It was just a disaster. I made most of my lap time in sector 1, but from sector 1 until the end of the lap I was slower than on the medium. It was just undriveable, I was losing the front end massively.

"We need to have a look because this is not normal, why there was so much degradation over one lap. The fronts were completely killed in the high-speed [corners]."

This happened particularly through the Esses, after which Hadjar had to pay the price for the remainder of the lap, according to Wache.

"With this type of lay-out, you have the full high-speed corners in sector 1, after Turn 1. And I think if you overcook the tyres there, it's more or less finished for the lap", Red Bull's technical director said.

Things naturally need to improve significantly for qualifying, although Hadjar took some confidence from Verstappen's day. Hadjar remains hopeful that he can turn the situation around with fresh set-up changes before parc ferme conditions come into effect at the start of qualifying.

"Yes, I mean, if they manage to do it on the other side… The [tyre] temperatures are just sky-high, but we are running at the same speeds in those corners. So we need to tweak something on the car balance. We were running different things to try, but to have such a bad feeling, I'm a bit surprised to be honest."

articles.title: Angel Reese’s hairstylist explains the WNBA superstar’s look
articles.summary: So far, the Atlanta Dream star has taken control of the WNBA Finals — and stayed firmly in control of the latest, flowing version of her always show-stopping hair.
articles.body: Angel Reese has always known the power of an image. For as long as the basketball star has been in the public eye — as the LSU “Bayou Barbie” and now as the “Queen of the South” for the Atlanta Dream — she has always glammed up for games: nails done, face beat, edges laid, and long hair pulled back and secured with a headband. (“I have a hair stylist in every city,” she once said.) While Reese has played with her look over the course of the season — see her bright pink wig during this year’s All-Star weekend, or her braids during September’s FIBA World Cup — her ever-changing hair has become a signature, enough to make headlines on its own. During Reese’s first two years in the league, while playing with the Chicago Sky, she’d graced magazine covers and rubbed elbows with A-listers at the Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show and the Met Gala. On the court, though, despite her leading the league in rebounds per game, the Sky had two losing seasons and zero playoff appearances, and her exit from the team wasn’t exactly on the best terms. But in her debut season with Atlanta, she’s won Defensive Player of the Year, a career-defining honor, and led her team to the WNBA Finals against the Golden State Valkyries. Her work at both ends of the court — including dropping a shocking 30 points in Game 2 against the league’s best defense — has led the Dream to a dominant start in the series. And even as she bullies the Valkyries, her hair remains soft. When she runs, the locks bounce against her back, floating behind her when she kicks up the speed. When she jumps for a block or rebound, her hair jumps, too, momentarily creating a wavy halo around her head. Even when she briefly lost her headband during Game 3 in Atlanta, giving the top of her head a slight pouf, the result was less messy Elizabeth Holmes and more a statement of her hair’s power. It can’t — shouldn’t! — be tamed. A month ago, the Atlanta-based stylist Jamal Brice installed her current look: a black, wavy sew-in with raw Cambodian hair, from a hair brand owned by one of her close friends. (For sew-ins, the natural hair is braided down against the scalp and the added hair is sewn into the braids.) “She wanted to keep it in the playoffs,” said Brice. He added, “And the Finals.” Styling hair for athletes comes with challenges. In a scramble for the ball, opponents might pull hair. Players fling themselves across the floor or are hit in the head. Wigs have fallen off mid-game. On Thursday, between Game 3 and Game 4, Brice explained how he got Reese ready for the sport’s biggest stage. This conversation has been edited and condensed for clarity. How does the way you style Reese’s hair for the season differ from non-basketball events? Different events call for different things. For basketball season — whether she’s getting a ponytail or whether she’s getting a traditional sew-in — she always gets the sew-in for security purposes. She rarely wears wigs during the season. She has worn wigs, like the pink one for the Barbie game, that one was a wig. But she doesn’t really keep those in as long as she would wear a sew-in. Most of the collabs that we’ve done, as far as Reebok, the CFDAs, the Met Gala, most of those were wigs. What makes a sew-in better for athletes? A wig is held down by an adhesive, so with sweat and makeup and whatever else, it’s more likely for a wig to slide back or move or readjust. That can be tricky. Typically, people who work out don’t wear wigs. They typically wear sew-ins or braids, because it’s not likely for a sew-in to just come out of your head because you’re sweating or anything like that. With Angel playing games, a wig probably would last maybe two or three days, because of sweat, oils and things like that, which doesn’t really work well with the glue. When’s the last time you guys did a touch-up? Typically, Angel gets her hair touched up weekly or maybe three times a month. I just touched up her hair today. She does not get her hair done on game days. I know a lot of athletes that want to stick to a certain routine so that they’re focused during the game or on game days. I think it’s just one of those rituals where she doesn’t want to do anything. She wants to chill and just be focused. What do you do during these touch-ups? She can change the style sometimes. Sew-ins do get loose, the threading could get loose, so sometimes you can get a touch-up and you can get it tightened back up. That’s what we did today. She has this loose wavy hair in right now, so she could either wear it wet or she could wear it blown out and curled or pressed, whatever she decides. So it’s changing the style, and fixing things about it, like if it needs to be tightened, or her roots or something like that need to be cleaned. And how long does that take? Maybe like an hour. In the WNBA, I see a lot of locs, a lot of braids, but I don’t see as many sew-ins. Have you noticed that, too? Yes, for sure. People have personal preferences, so whatever fits the player, I feel like that’s what they go with. For Angel, I would say she has more of this feminine energy, this super girly energy, on and off the court. She loves her weaves. She loves to keep her hair done. She also takes very good care of her natural hair. Angel has always been a hair girl, even before me. I think that that’s why she loves her sew-ins, or quick weaves, or weaves, or ponytails. I’ve noticed during the playoffs, she has her ends tied a lot. Why? It’s mainly so that the hair doesn’t go into her face. That’s also why she wears the headbands, so that the hair isn’t in her face. Because ideally, if she took her hair out of the hair tie, or if she took the headband off, it does lay toward her face. You mentioned she embraces this super girly energy. With her look now, what do you think it says about where she is as a player or in her career? I feel like she always gave this feminine energy. She always felt like she’s that girl, because she is. I feel like she exudes that, on and off the court. Angel knows exactly who she is, and that’s something that I love about her. Hair is always evolving, so I feel like she’s always evolving. She’s always growing.

articles.title: Jacksonville Jaguars studs and duds at the bye week
articles.summary: With the bye week here for the Jaguars, let's take a look back at some of the standout performers through six games.
articles.body:
With the bye week in full swing for the Jacksonville Jaguars , let's take a look back at some of the standout performers through the first six games of the season.

Here are three players who have stood out, and two players/areas where the Jaguars will need more second-half production.

Parker Washington ended the 2025 season red-hot, and he picked up this year right where he left off. Washington has continued to be a go-to target for Trevor Lawrence and a big-play threat for the Jaguars offense. Through six games, he's caught 26 passes for 416 yards with four touchdowns. Of those catches, 15 have gone for first downs.

It's becoming increasingly difficult to figure out where Thomas Jr. fits in this Jaguars' offense. His playing time and opportunities have been decreasing, including playing only 15 snaps against Houston. Thomas Jr. has caught just 9 of 18 passes this season for 105 yards and a score. He has no catches over the last two games.

Having a steady run game to lean on is a key element of the Liam Coen offense, and even with imperfect blocking around him, Tuten has often provided that. On 94 carries, Tuten has totaled 388 rushing yards at 4.1 yards per rush with two scores. He's been terrific at making defenders miss, averaging 3.62 yards after contact, while generating 25 missed tackles. Tuten has been a factor in the pass game as well.

It's hard to nitpick the defensive performance, but creating more sacks is one area where this unit can really improve. On the season, the Jaguars have just 11 sacks through six games, which ranks tied for 20th in the NFL. The Jaguars are giving themselves opportunities, totaling the 10th-most QB pressures, but are failing to convert those plays into sacks at a similar rate.

We are starting to see the emergence of Travis Hunter on both sides of the ball. On defense has handled a full workload, allowing 16 receptions on 26 targets, with very good ball production, totaling two end zone interceptions and three pass breakups. Quarterbacks have a passer rating of 58.8 when targeting him. On offense, Hunter's role has remained small, but he was a big factor against Houston, with four receptions in nine plays, which included scoring a touchdown.

articles.title: Así está la pelea por el número uno de Premier Padel: Chingotto y Galán necesitan un milagro
articles.standfirst: Coello y Tapia podrían cerrar la pelea virtualmente en el Major de Kuwait, mientras que Ale y Fede tienen muy pocas opciones
articles.summary: Coello y Tapia podrían cerrar la pelea virtualmente en el Major de Kuwait, mientras que Ale y Fede tienen muy pocas opciones
articles.body: La batalla por ser la mejor pareja del año en el pádel profesional en la categoría masculina ha perdido cierta emoción en las últimas semanas con la racha de Arturo Coello y Agustín Tapia. Hasta el Major de París reinaba la igualdad, pero las distancias se han incrementado con los recientes éxitos de los ‘Golden Boys’. Sin embargo, todavía quedan opciones matemáticas para Fede Chingotto y Ale Galán, aunque ya no dependen de sí mismos y necesitan un milagro para darle la vuelta a esta situación. La próxima semana se celebra el Major de Kuwait, la categoría de torneo que más puntos reparte en el calendario. Justo después llegarán el P1 de Dubái, el Major de México y, para terminar, el Tour Finals de Barcelona. Cuatro citas, 6.500 puntos en juego y una diferencia en la Race que actualmente es de 2.840 puntos entre Arturo y Agustín (cada uno) con respecto a sus inmediatos perseguidores. Llegando a todas las finales, Coello y Tapia seguirían siendo números uno por segundo año consecutivo. Pese a no ganar ninguna y aunque Ale y Fede se llevaran los cuatro títulos, la distancia entre ellos seguiría siendo de 240 puntos por jugador. Los de Jorge Martínez tendrían que ganarlo todo y esperar un tropiezo de los ‘Golden Boys’ para acabar el año en lo más alto de la clasificación. Un escenario muy improbable y curioso sería que Ale y Fede se llevaran las cuatro citas y que sus rivales llegaran a todas las finales menos a una: la de Dubái, donde caerían en semifinales. Esa combinación de resultados terminaría con ambas duplas empatadas a puntos, algo que nunca ha sucedido en la historia de este deporte. Lo más favorable para Chingotto y Galán sería ganar en Kuwait y que Arturo y Agustín tuvieran una derrota tempranera en dieciseisavos u octavos de final. De esa forma se recortarían las distancias y podrían ver radicalmente aumentadas sus posibilidades de terminar remontando, aunque la realidad es que llegan en una mala racha de tres torneos seguidos sin llegar a la final y que los de Gustavo Pratto nunca han caído tan pronto en un torneo de esta categoría. Del otro lado, los ‘Golden Boys’ lo tienen bastante factible para acabar con esta pelea mucho antes de lo previsto. Pese al elevado número de puntos que se reparten en estas cuatro citas que quedan para acabar la temporada en Premier Padel, Coello y Tapia podrían sellar matemáticamente su liderato en el siguiente torneo. Ganando en Kuwait, la pelea no estaría acabada del todo, pero sí serían virtualmente los ganadores de esta temporada. Levantando este Major, les valdría casi con presentarse a lo demás para mantener el trono de este deporte. Matemáticamente tendrían que levantar el título esta semana y que Chingotto y Galán perdieran en octavos de final o antes. En caso de que los de Jorge Martínez llegaran más lejos, tendrían que esperar al P1 de Dubái para terminar. En cualquier caso, el ‘King’ y el ‘Mozart’ lo tienen muy de cara para ser los dominadores del circuito una temporada más, mientras que Ale y Fede necesitan un milagro para mantener vivas sus esperanzas de completar una hazaña épica que llevan buscando desde que se juntaron. El próximo torneo podría dictar sentencia o postergar el fin de esta batalla.

articles.title: Report – Napoli Identify January Transfer Targets as Allegri Seeks Four New Signings
articles.summary: Napoli have already begun planning for the January transfer window, with Massimiliano Allegri keen to strengthen several positions after a frustrating summer...
articles.body:
Napoli have already begun planning for the January transfer window, with Massimiliano Allegri keen to strengthen several positions after a frustrating summer. According to Gazzetta dello Sport , president Aurelio De Laurentiis and sporting director Giovanni Manna are working alongside the Italian manager to address the squad's shortcomings.

Around a dozen players will be over 30 by next June, prompting Napoli to prioritize younger profiles. The Partenopei are targeting a new right-back to provide cover for captain Giovanni Di Lorenzo, while another center-back remains a possibility despite Rafa Marin's return to contention and Benoit Badiashile's encouraging progress.

However, that would only be the beginning of a comprehensive overhaul at the Diego Maradona Stadium.

Napoli could revive their interest in Fiorentina right-back Dodo, whose contract expires next summer. The Brazilian has struggled for regular playing time in Florence, potentially opening the door to a January move. Udinese defender Oumar Solet also remains a name to watch.

Allegri also wants to reinforce midfield and attack. Mamadou Coulibaly, the 22-year-old Monaco midfielder, features on Napoli's shortlist, although his valuation could complicate negotiations. Rennes star Sebastian Szymanski represents another option thanks to his versatility and experience across several European leagues.

Frank Zambo Anguissa's uncertain future could also influence Napoli's plans, with the midfielder approaching the final months of his contract. If an offer arrives in January, the club could consider selling him rather than risk losing him for nothing next summer.

Up front, much will depend on Lorenzo Lucca, who has struggled to live up to his substantial price tag since joining Napoli from Udinese. Allegri wants a reliable alternative to Rasmus Hojlund, allowing the Danish striker to rest without weakening the attack.

articles.title: Bayern Munich issue further Vincent Kompany update after collapse at training ground
articles.summary: Bayern sporting director Max Eberl said the club would need to ‘protect’ their head coach and ensure he focuses on recovering
articles.body:
Bayern Munich expect Vincent Kompany to be absent for "weeks" rather than days following his collapse at the club's training ground on Friday.

Kompany was taken to hospital after falling ill during team training , having been unwell with a viral infection during the week.

Bayern's sporting director Max Eberl told a press conference on Saturday that Kompany remains in a "stable" condition in hospital.

Despite his illness, the former Manchester City and Belgium captain was on the touchline for Wednesday's 2-2 draw against Arsenal.

And Eberl said Bayern would now need to look to "protect" their head coach and Kompany will be given as much time as he needs to recover.

"We're not starting to put together any timeframes," Eberl said ahead of Sunday's game against Freiburg.

"We need to firstly figure out what it is and then we'll discuss calmly what recovery time is to be.

"We won't be talking about days, but weeks. We need to all be clear on that."

Kompany's assistant coach, the Englishman Aaron Danks, will take charge of Bayern's Bundesliga match against Freiburg.

Danks said he had spoken to Kompany but had not discussed this weekend's match as the priority was his recovery from the virus.

"I explained to him that we wouldn't be having no football conversations," Danks said. "It was just checking in on his health and making sure he's OK.

"All the football operations are in our hands and we'll work together as a team to keep the club moving forward."

Kompany had admitted following the draw with the Gunners that he had not listened to his body by taking time off work.

"I caught a pretty nasty virus last week, and of course I didn't listen to my body," Kompany said on Wednesday.

"And then at some point my body just said: 'Enough is enough."
