articles.title: Mavericks fans demand punishment for Aaron Nesmith after Pacers star sends Cooper Flagg to locker room
articles.summary: Dallas Mavericks star Cooper Flagg had to sit out for the entire second half of the game as he suffered a shoulder injury due to Aaron Nesmith’s reckless fou...
articles.body:
Dallas Mavericks star Cooper Flagg had to sit out for the entire second half of the game as he suffered a shoulder injury due to Aaron Nesmith's reckless foul on him towards the end of the second quarter.

Flagg was leading a fast break and on his way to score an easy basket. Nesmith followed Flagg and tried to get the block but, in the process, the Mavs star awkwardly landed on the floor, which led to an injury.

A scuffle broke out as the Mavericks players were angered by what Nesmith had done on the play. The score was 73-40 with less than a minute to play in the second quarter. It seemed like the Pacers guard fouled in frustration as Flagg was dominating the game, scoring 14 points but also stuffing the stat sheet with 5 rebounds, 6 assists and 3 steals.

He had a team high +/- of 34, which indicated how effective Flagg was on the night, but after falling awkwardly, he was unable to return to the game.

Fans want harsh punishment for Aaron Nesmith

Nesmith was punished with a Flagrant 1 foul and also given a technical for indulging in a scuffle with the Mavericks players. Naji Marshall was also handed a technical as he came in heated, trying to retaliate against Nesmith. The two had to be separated, which further increased the intensity of the game.

After the first half, it was reported that Flagg had suffered an injury to his left shoulder.

Despite the injury to their star, the Mavs took home a 121-105 win in Tyrese Haliburton's return to Indiana.

While Mavericks fans were happy to grab their first win of the season, they wanted major repercussions for Nesmith as he caused the injury to Flagg.

"Nesmith needs a 25-game suspension after that b*******," said one fan. While another added: "This dude is way too wild I loved his game and knew he'd be a decent player but he's way too crazy."

Someone also wrote: "This is such a dangerous and dirty play."

Another fan opined: "This should mean multiple games of suspension for Nesmith. What a cowardly c***, could have really f***** Flagg up."

"There's absolutely no need to make that foul when you're down 30+," added an account user on X.

Nesmith will have to pay a small amount for the technical foul he was assessed, along with Marshall. However, the league has not confirmed whether he would be further suspended for the play or would be fined. If Nesmith was assessed a Flagrant 2, he would have to immediately leave the game, but even then he would not be suspended as per NBA's rules.

articles.title: ‘You fell off’ – Kobe Bryant’s ex-teammate destroys Linda Cohn’s attempted jab at LeBron James

articles.body:
Former ESPN expert Linda Cohn gets brutally called out for her take on LeBron James' viral US National Anthem controversy.

Philadelphia 76ers star LeBron James is facing massive backlash for allegedly practicing his golf swing during the US National Anthem ahead of the team's game against the Cleveland Cavaliers.

Despite Donald Trump calling out James' actions, the 41-year-old simply brushed it off. However, the media refuses to forgive James for disrespecting America.

Former ESPN analyst Linda Cohn became the latest name to take a jab at the King, but she was quickly called out by Kobe Bryant's former teammate Matt Barnes.

Matt Barnes snaps at Linda Cohn for ignoring Donald Trump to take a shot at LeBron James

During a recent episode of her podcast, Cohn called out James for acting like a 'three-year-old kid' who couldn't stand still during the US National Anthem.

While Cohn thought she did the right thing by calling out the 4x NBA champion, she was quickly given a reality check by several big names, including Barnes.

"You have more issue w Bron doing this than you do w Trump s_______ on the people of this country. D___ you fell off," Matt Barnes wrote on Instagram.

Barnes wasn't alone in calling out Cohn; even Hollywood star Jamie Foxx snapped at the former ESPN personality for trying to 'bash' LeBron while hoping to become relevant again.

It will be interesting to see how the 66-year-old will respond to being called irrelevant over her James comments. Will she back down and apologise? Only time will tell.

articles.title: Jemele Hill calls out James Dolan’s ‘utterly despicable’ behaviour with Knicks staff
articles.summary: The New York Knicks players received their championship rings earlier this week but a lot of staff at Madison Square Garden are not expected to be given one....
articles.body:
The New York Knicks players received their championship rings earlier this week but a lot of staff at Madison Square Garden are not expected to be given one.

After a 53-year wait, the Knicks won the NBA championship by beating the San Antonio Spurs in this year's Finals.

The roster was subsequently handed their rings ahead of the season-opener against the Philadelphia 76ers. But The Athletic have now reported that the Knicks' assistant coaches did not get rings this week, while many employees at Madison Square Garden will not receive rings at all.

They stated: "The Knicks' assistant coaches did not receive their championship rings during Tuesday's ceremony, despite being handed ring boxes, according to league sources. Many longtime employees at Madison Square Garden will not receive rings at all, per team sources. Those employees got their hopes up in late September, when they were sent a fake championship ring offer as part of a phishing test."

Jemele Hill has now responded to that tweet from The Athletic to hit out at James Dolan.

She wrote: "James Dolan is determined to kill every good vibe around this team, and bring every piece of bad karma their way.

"This is just utterly despicable. He makes it so hard to want good things for the Knicks because he has such a long history of treating people so poorly."

Fans have also called out Dolan about the phishing email previously mentioned by The Athletic.

In the meantime, the Knicks are still searching for their first win of the season after losing to the Boston Celtics on Friday.

articles.title: Tennessee Titans vs. Cleveland Browns: Week 7 staff picks and predictions
articles.summary: The Titans Wire staff offer their picks and predictions ahead of a Week 7 game between the Tennessee Titans and Cleveland Browns.
articles.body:
The Tennessee Titans (1-5) will take on the Cleveland Browns (4-2) this Sunday afternoon at Nissan Stadium in their seventh game of the 2026 regular season.

Opening the week, the Titans were listed as 2-point home underdogs , but that line has shifted slightly with Tennessee now at +2.5 as of this writing.

How does the Titans Wire staff see this Week 7 battle shaking out? Here's a look at our picks and score predictions.

In what promises to be a defensive battle, the upstart Browns come into Nashville poised to continue their hot streak, but they'll run into a Titans franchise high off their first win. The Titans' offensive line will give Cam Ward just enough protection to hit paydirt, and the Titans' defense will force Deshaun Watson into multiple turnovers that decide the game. Tennessee pulls out a close 17-13 win over the Browns.

The Titans have had a chaotic week. They got their first win of the season and barely got to enjoy it before the Jordan Elliott incident came to light. They've had a few days to get through that now, and if Robert Saleh is doing his job, the players aren't even thinking about that anymore. The Browns have surprised me this season; the way Todd Monken has them playing is impressive. Their defense is going to be a problem for the Titans' offense, and if the Titans don't get out in front early, the Browns' defense will shut them down. However, the Browns can't sleep on the Titans' defense either, which hasn't let any team score more than 26 points this season. It's going to be a defensive battle throughout the game, and whichever defense holds out the longest is the team that wins. Considering the Titans' inability to win back-to-back games, I'm giving the edge to the Browns.

The Titans have made me look like a fool two weeks running, so take any prediction I make with a grain of salt at this point. However, with the offense starting to groove a bit, I think they'll win their second consecutive game against a Browns team that struggles to score and consistently finds themselves in close games. The home field advantage will give Tennessee the edge.

Can the Titans make it two in a row? The Browns are playing pretty solid football. They have a good defense, which will make life tough for Cam Ward and the Titans. I expect a low-scoring affair with Cleveland winning.

Coming off a six-sack performance, the Titans defense faces a Browns offense that has allowed Deshaun Watson to be the most sacked QB in the NFL this season. With the Titans gaining momentum with 19 second-half points in Indianapolis, expect another complementary level from all three phases to pull off another upset.

The Cleveland Browns have a legitimate opportunity to take down the Tennessee Titans this week, and it starts with a defense that has consistently given opposing offenses problems. Cleveland is allowing just 20.3 points per game and has recorded 19 sacks through six games, giving the Browns a major advantage against a Titans offense that has struggled to find consistency. With Deshaun Watson leading the offense and Quinshon Judkins expected to be available, Cleveland has an opportunity to establish the run, control the clock, and keep Tennessee's defense on the field. Although the Titans are coming off an impressive comeback victory over Indianapolis, the Browns have proven they can win close games, and if their defensive front can pressure Cam Ward and force a few mistakes, Cleveland should have what it takes to leave Nashville with another victory.

Even with the Titans coming off their first win, their struggling offense is going to have trouble against the Browns' defense. The Browns might very well be the surprise of the league at 4-2 so far. The Browns have won four of their last five, and I expect that to continue against the Titans on Sunday.

Katie Boulter has lost in the Japan Open semi-finals, in her first match since reclaiming the British number one spot from Sonny Kartal.

Kartal moved above Boulter in the world rankings by reaching the final of last week's Wuhan Open.

Eighth seed Boulter rallied after being swept aside in the opening set, going a break up at the start of the second.

But Siniakova, also 30, maintained her bid for a first singles title in four years by claiming two hard-fought breaks of her own to wrap up victory in 85 minutes.

She will now play 2023 champion Ashlyn Krueger in Sunday's final after the 22-year-old American beat compatriot and top seed Ann Li 6-4 6-7 (4-7) 6-3.

articles.title: After reflection, Giants' Cam Skattebo says recent fumbles a mental issue
articles.summary: New York Giants RB Cam Skattebo took a week to reflect on his recent fumbles and attributed them to a mental issue, not a technique issue.
articles.body:
New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo said he used the past week to step back and address the mental side of his recent ball-security issues rather than treating them as a technique problem.

"I think I got taught a lesson," Skattebo told reporters on Friday. "I don't know if that's from them or from myself, but I kind of had to step back and look at it and figure out why I was doing the things I was doing, what was happening. Came to practice, corrected those things, worked on them. Ready to go back out there and play ball."

He described getting ahead of himself in some games this season and losing sight of the primary task at that moment.

"There were a couple of mishaps that happened and I think it was the mental part," Skattebo said. "You see, in (the Washington) game, I got really excited, really happy. I think I got a little ahead of myself during the end of that game. I lost the main purpose of the game, and it was to take care of the ball at that moment. And I lost it. I think just understanding the situation and the circumstances I'm in, taking care of the ball and I'll be fine."

Skattebo made clear he is not positioning himself for a larger role based on this week's work. He said he has not yet done anything to earn more responsibility and will simply maximize whatever snaps come his way Sunday.

"I didn't do anything yet," Skattebo said. "I took care of the ball during practice and whatever my role is on Sunday is going to be my role and I'm going to give it everything I've got."

That approach fits with how the running back group has responded to John Harbaugh's open competition for the workhorse job. Skattebo said he, Devin Singletary, and Tyrone Tracy Jr. entered the week with a shared mindset and have stayed in regular communication about how each likes to hit holes so the next man is prepared when one comes off the field.

"Whoever is going to carry the ball knows that the other two guys got their back," Skattebo said. "When that guy comes off the field, the next guy in is going to perform. The vibes have been great. We've been talking. We've been staying on the same page."

The three backs have also coordinated with the offensive line so blocking schemes and preferred paths stay aligned. Skattebo said that communication has been consistent this week and the group is ready to carry it into the game.

articles.title: 4 NHL Trade Ideas for the Teams That Missed Out on Connor Hellebuyck
articles.summary: The Connor Hellebuyck saga is finally over with Friday's trade that sent him from the Winnipeg Jets to the New Jersey Devils.
articles.body:
The Connor Hellebuyck saga is finally over with Friday's trade that sent him from the Winnipeg Jets to the New Jersey Devils.

While it is a huge deal for the Devils and could open a new window for Stanley Cup contention for them, an almost equally intriguing story is what the teams that missed out on Hellebuyck might do for a goalie option.

So let's take a look at a few teams that could have been in the running for Hellebuyck and try to come up with some options to help them fill their potential goalie needs.

The idea: Trade for Montreal Canadiens goalie Sam Montembeault

Not that the Rangers were ever seriously in the market for Hellebuyck given his contract situation, but they could be interested in adding another goalie given the season-ending injury to starter Igor Shesterkin.

They have recently been linked to Utah's Karel Vejmelka and Buffalo's Ukka-Pekka Luukkonen, but a lot of that could have been dependent on one of those teams actually landing Hellebuyck and no longer needing either goalie.

Both goalies are signed long-term to contracts worth north of $4 million per season.

While those are not small numbers, they should be manageable for long-term backups as the salary cap continues to rise.

The question is whether or not the Rangers actually need that.

Shesterkin is obviously locked in as their starter when he returns next season, and rookie Dylan Garand is showing he has a chance to be a viable NHL goalie and extremely cheap backup. Why give up more significant assets and take up more salary cap space if you don't need to do it?

What might make more sense for the Rangers is simply finding a short-term, rental option for the rest of this season.

One name that could be available and make sense: Montreal's Sam Montembeault. The Canadiens have two young goalies that they really like in Jakub Dobes and Jacob Fowler that should be the future, while Montembeault is in the final year of his contract and likely the odd man out. He has had some really good seasons in the past, and could be a solid veteran to accompany Garand for the foreseeable future.

The value here shouldn't be anything more than a draft pick.

Let's say the Rangers send one of their four third-round picks over the next two years and a later pick to the Canadiens for Montembeault.

The trade idea: Alexander Nikishin to Minnesota for Filip Gustavsson

Even though the Hurricanes have won over the years without making major investments in the goalie position, they were still a potential player for Hellebuyck and would have been a fascinating landing spot. It would have given Hellebuyck one of the best defensive teams to play behind that he has ever had in the NHL, and would have almost certainly made them the favorites to win a second straight Stanley Cup.

But the Hurricanes were not willing to meet Winnipeg's asking price in terms of forwards, which currently leaves them with Pyotr Kochetkov and Brandon Bussi in their net.

While Bussi played well enough to help them win the Cup a year ago, there are still some legitimate questions as to whether or not he can do that over a full season. He is off to a slow start so far this season and is far from a sure-thing as a regular option.

A goalie upgrade could be in the cards here, even if it is not one that is as exciting or impactful as Hellebuyck.

The great thing for Carolina is its system is so structured, so well played, and so steady that it really doesn't need a goalie that has to steal a lot of games. It just requires a goalie that will not lose games. There are a couple of intriguing veteran trade options out there.

One of the most intriguing: Minnesota's Filip Gustavsson.

Jesper Wallstedt has become the No. 1 starter in Minnesota, and while the Wild might like the idea of keeping both Wallstedt and Gustavsson long-term, that's probably not viable financially given Gustavsson's $6.8 million cap hit over the next four-and-a-half seasons and whatever Wallstedt's next contract looks like (probably not cheap).

Carolina has a great trade chip in defenseman Alexander Nikishin, and Minnesota might be in the market for a longer-term, young defense option given the uncertainty around the future of Quinn Hughes. Not that Nikishin would be a suitable Hughes replacement, but he certainly still has some untapped potential that could be of interest to the Wild.

He remains unsigned in Carolina as a restricted free agent, and it only seems to be a matter of when and where he gets traded as opposed to if he gets traded. Why not use him as part of a trade to get a long-term goalie option? Gustavsson has had some big years during his career and could do well playing behind Carolina's defensive structure.

The trade idea: 3-team trade idea involving Stuart Skinner and Karel Vejmelka

Utah missed out on one Winnipeg goalie, but maybe it could get a different one?

And maybe it could use that as an opportunity to move Karel Vejmelka's contract to another team (the Los Angeles Kings) that also missed out on Hellebuyck this week.

Here's how it works: Los Angeles trades Alex Turcotte to Winnipeg for Stuart Skinner, and then turns around and trades Skinner to Utah for Vejmelka.

You can throw in some draft pick compensation from each team to sweeten the pot as needed, but this is the bones of it. It allows a couple of players that might need a change of scenery to get one, and Utah gets to try a different goalie that, while inconsistent, is capable of putting together decent stretches when used correctly.

Winnipeg currently has three goalies on its NHL roster after the Hellebuyck trade, with Nico Daws joining Skinner and Clay Stevenson. That is probably not going to work long-term, and something is going to have to give. Stevenson is a talented player that should get an extended look before they have to make a decision on him as an unrestricted free agent after the season, and this would open the door for him to do that. While Skinner has had a nice start to the season, that might actually make him the most tradable goalie of the three still on Winnipeg's roster. Especially if it falls out of playoff contention as the season goes on.

Turcotte has simply not panned out as hoped in Los Angeles and could use a fresh start somewhere else. Even after adding Dawson Mercer in the Hellebuyck trade, Winnipeg should still be in the market for more forward depth, and Turcotte could be a low-risk, high-reward gamble.

Utah obviously has a lot of belief in Sebastian Cossa after trading a first-round pick for him over the summer, while its organizational belief in Vejmelka might be starting to fade given his struggles and general inconsistency over the past couple of years. Skinner doesn't exactly solve the inconsistency concern, but he is a cheaper option, on a shorter contract, and could create some more long-term flexibility.

The Kings have two veteran goalies on their roster in Darcy Kuemper and Anton Forsberg, but neither player has been close to good enough this season and both players are unrestricted free agents after this season. For all of their flaws, the Kings generally defend well and could create a favorable situation for Vejmelka to get back on the right track. The Kings mostly need a goalie that isn't going to lose games for them. It is a low bar, and one that should not be difficult to reach.

The Sabres might end up regretting not doing more to get Hellebuyck.

After a quiet offseason that only saw them subtract talent from the roster instead of adding to it, the Sabres are off to a slow start and have more questions than answers in net. Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen has not played well, and seems to be a complete wild-card every season when it comes to what his performance will look like.

Getting a player like Hellebuyck would have not only been a boost to the roster, it would have given the fan base a needed lift as well. These people watched 14 years of rancid hockey, got a taste of success during the 2025-26 season, and were rewarded by a shockingly quiet and disappointing offseason that did nothing to make the NHL team better in the short-term.

There are not many great long-term options on the trade market right now for goalies, so the Sabres might have to turn their attention to more short-term options.

There a handful of pending UFA's that could be on their radar, ranging from Detroit's John Gibson, to Seattle's Philipp Grubauer, to St. Louis' Jordan Binnington.

Binnington is the option they should avoid.

But Gibson and Grubauer have had some solid performances in recent years behind sub-par defensive teams, and could both be on the market if their teams slip out of playoff contention (as both very easily could do over the coming weeks and months).

In both cases we might be talking about draft pick capital going back the other way, and probably not significant draft pick capital. Maybe a second-round pick. At most. Maybe a third-round pick and a later pick, or lower-tier prospect. It would not be an overly exciting move, and certainly not as exciting as Hellebuyck would have been, but it could at least offer a little bit of stability to a position that might be lacking it. At least for the short-term.

articles.title: Booking Rey Mysterio's Best Opponents For Rumored WWE Retirement Tour
articles.summary: When thinking of possible upcoming WWE retirements, Rey Mysterio doesn't top the list.
articles.body:
When thinking of possible upcoming WWE retirements, Rey Mysterio doesn't top the list.

But Mysterio has always had a way of jumping over things and stealing shows in a way that landed him in the WWE Hall of Fame, among his many accolades.

From the sounds of it, Mysterio is the big name hanging up the boots in 2027.

According to WrestleVotes Radio (h/t Sean Rueter of Cageside Seats), there has already been some motion in WWE as to how the company would present Mysterio's retirement in the ring next year.

Booking Mysterio's goodbye isn't that difficult. But this is WWE. Neither was John Cena's and we all saw how that went. Everyone also sees how so-so the booking has been since for Gunther, the guy doing the retiring.

Mysteiro will turn 52 in December and he's been on record saying that his body's slowing down, bringing his in-ring career to a close. Luckily for him (and fans), his farewell tour won't demand major in-ring stress.

After all, Mysterio is currently an on-screen AAA general manager. Bringing that role back to weekly WWE programming on one of the three big shows makes a bunch of sense.

Family helps here. Mysterio's daughter, Aalyah, is training at the WWE Performance Center. Using Mysterio in an almost managerial or mentor role to help introduce her to crowds properly would be a shrewd way to go, even if it's just on NXT episodes.

Of course, onlookers want to know about the in-ring stuff more.

The conversation must start with Dominik Mysterio. They've had their brush-ups before, since his son really started going on the active roster back in 2020 (has it really been that long already?). Those two linking up again is a must.

A lot of Cena's farewell tour was rekindling old, classic feuds. Even if it's just backstage segments or in-ring promos with surprises like Batista, Kurt Angle and Undertaker, to name a very few, it would be a nice ode to his legendary career. Add Randy Orton's name to Dominik's when it comes to actual matches, of course.

The other element of Cena's goodbye tour was paying it forward, or the so-called passing the torch. That's where the in-ring stuff would really come from with Mysterio.

It's timely, too. Amid Penta's shocking rise to Money in the Bank briefcase winner, Wrestling Observer Radio's Dave Meltzer (h/t WrestleZone's Ojas Kulkarni ) suggested that WWE is changing its approach to the better for Mexican stars.

Meaning, names like Penta, Dragon Lee or even a revived Sin Cara character, to name a very few, never mind the AAA ties now, could be viable options for this sort of idea.

Granted, all of this assumes Mysterio goes on a "tour" at all. Cena was an anomaly on this front. Maybe it's a one-off match, which means it would go to Dominik.

A fun idea there might be a "mask" or even career match. Obvious result, but it's felt obvious for about six years now that Dominik would be the one to retire Mysterio.

If WWE wants to really WWW'ify it, though, they could have their cake and eat it too by involving Gunther. The career-killing Gunther trying to cut in line and brutalizing Mysterio before Dominik makes the save and gets his own feud could put everyone over.

Speaking of putting people over, all of Mysterio's last match would be about Dominik. It's no secret he's had a mid year or so on the main roster. Morphing back into a beloved babyface by saving his dad, or going super-heat heel by stealing the mask…it all just works. It's not hard to pull off either route and, frankly, everyone already knows the actual matches will be classics.

One could argue for Penta doing the retiring, but the man is already main eventing specials in Mexico against Roman Reigns and winning briefcases. For all we know, he's going to shock win a top title very soon. He doesn't need the help at this point.

Fittingly, Mysterio's value to cruiserweights and the art of lucha libre around the globe is unquestioned. It would only be right that he uses his official goodbye to jump start Dominik's rise to the main-event scene to carry on in his stead.

articles.body: Luis Calzado fue elegido como mejor portero del mundo por la Federación Internacional de Hockey (FIH). Es el primer guardameta español que recibe este galardón. Otros jugadores nacionales sí habían sido reconocidos en otras categorías como Pol Amat, mejor jugador del mundo en 2008, o Santi Freixa, mejor joven en 2004. “Recibir el premio a mejor portero del mundo es un honor enorme. Pero, cuando pienso en lo que significa este reconocimiento, es inevitable echar la vista atrás y pensar en todo el camino que me ha traído hasta aquí”, explica Calzado, que comparte el premio con los compañeros, técnicos y personas que le han acompañado durante su trayectoria. El galardón llega en un año en el que se marchó a Países Bajos Después de desarrollar toda su carrera en el RC Polo, Calzado fichó por el SV Kampong con el que se proclamó campeón de la Euroliga tras imponerse en la final al Gantoise belga. "Este premio es el reflejo de un camino mucho más largo. Desde mis años en el Polo, que han sido fundamentales para formarme como jugador y como profesional, hasta todo lo vivido esta temporada. Ha sido un año exigente, con momentos complicados y mucho aprendizaje, pero también un año de grandes experiencias y de momentos inolvidables, como ganar la EHL”, señala Calzado. A la conquista de la EHL se sumó la medalla de plata conseguida con España en el Mundial, donde los RedSticks volvieron a disputar una final 28 años después. Un éxito colectivo que el guardameta considera un impulso para el futuro de la selección y una muestra del potencial de este grupo. "Con la selección, cerrar el año con una plata mundial tiene un significado enorme. Es algo que va mucho más allá del resultado. Es una motivación enorme para este grupo de locos, una señal de lo que podemos conseguir juntos y de las ganas que tenemos de seguir dando pasos adelante”, afirma Calzado.

articles.title: Inside BYU’s unique surge to the top of college football
articles.summary: BYU’s uniqueness isn’t its downfall, many inside and outside the school argue. Having an uncompromising identity is, in fact, its strength.
articles.body: The sun hadn’t yet risen over the Wasatch Range when Kalani Sitake decided to bust a move. Standing alongside Cosmo, the Brigham Young University mascot, the head football coach shimmied and shook ESPN’s “College GameDay” crew to commercial break, mixing steps from his native Tongan ritual dances with straight-up club vibing. On the other side of daylight, Sitake and his BYU football team would welcome No. 2 Notre Dame for arguably the biggest home game on campus in two decades. The Cougars are no beggars at the football feast. Jumpstarted by LaVell Edwards, the true father of the air raid offense, BYU has maintained national relevance through various conference iterations and even a dalliance with independence. But this was the Irish and all their golden-helmeted luster finding their way to Provo, Utah, for the first time since 2004, the enormity of their visit underscored by the pregame show luring people out before dawn. Yet with every eyeball trained on him and his team, there was Sitake, dancing like nobody was watching. The surprise samba left even hard-to-impress Nick Saban, whose rug cutting is limited to boot leg Cupid Shuffle videos on recruiting visits, near speechless. “My hat’s off to you,” Saban said. “You’re up here dancing before a game. I was so nervous before a big game, I couldn’t even spit.” Everything the Cougars are doing these days seems to spit in the eye of convention. Owned and operated by the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-Day Saints, a church that counts self-reliance and not spending more than it has among its core principles, BYU beat the Irish and currently is ranked No. 2 in the nation in an era of unchecked spending. Required to follow the church’s strict honor code that prohibits premarital sex, alcohol, tobacco, coffee and cursing, talented athletes are not just choosing BYU, they are opting to stay while elsewhere players are entering the transfer portal at the slightest hint of struggle. And, at a school, where 98% of the undergraduate population is Mormon and diversity is largely geography based, the Cougars are led by a quarterback who is Catholic-raised and the son of a Thai mother who named him Bear who, upon beating Notre Dame said, “We put our balls on the chopping block.” Yet asked to explain how BYU is getting over its host of limitations, those who work at, or have long been affiliated with, the school suggest people are looking at it all wrong. BYU’s uniqueness isn’t its downfall, they argue; having an uncompromising identity is, in fact, its strength. “In some ways, because of the realities of being a religious institution with firm beliefs and principles in the wild west of NIL, we have a clearer vision of what we can and can’t do and who we are,” said three-time Super Bowl champion Steve Young, a 1984 graduate of BYU. “In a sort of frictionless system, it’s about, who are you willing to be? We’re willing to be something unique. The complexity is really the beauty of it.” The new face of BYU Ryan Smith first started going to BYU games when he was still in diapers. His father, Scott, was a marketing research professor at the school and home football Saturdays in Provo weren’t optional. “It’s just what you did,” he told CNN Sports. Midway through his own undergrad career at BYU, Smith left school to join his father, who’d happened upon a startup concept involving a way to make sophisticated research more user friendly. As he was readying to launch Qualtrics, Scott Smith was diagnosed with throat cancer, so Ryan joined to help him see the project to fruition. In 2018, a German company bought Qualtrics for $8 billion. Smith has since bought the NBA’s Utah Jazz, relocated the Arizona Coyotes and turned them into Utah’s first NHL franchise, the Mammoth. He’s involved with Salt Lake’s MLS franchise and helped the city land the 2034 Winter Olympics. On Saturday, he tossed in an extra million bucks to sweeten the pot for the student kicker on “GameDay.” Smith is, in so many ways, the new face of BYU: a backward-ballcap-wearing dude who just so happens to rank No. 1,285 on Forbes’ list of billionaires. He is rich beyond measure, but a church member who believes fervently in its principles – actual proof that money and Mormonism do not have to be at odds. Which is the essential push/pull here. BYU long has viewed athletics as an integral part of its mission, intuitively understanding that a school that is constantly fighting misconceptions and stereotypes desperately needs the very American front porch of sports. “It opens a door to understand and learn who BYU is,” BYU president C. Shane Reese told CNN Sports. “A lot of people have not been to BYU or know anything about it. Football gives you a peek into who we are.” But the shift in college athletics has required an internal reconciling that is even more challenging than the external education. BYU at once wants to stay in line with its competition but doesn’t want to compromise who it is. Essentially, it wants to walk the impossible line between adhering to the staunch principle of tithing while simultaneously paying athletes millions to toss a ball around. “The most common question I get asked is, ‘What keeps you up at night?’” Reese said. “For sure I would say it’s the worry about us losing sight of who we are as an institution. Our strength is our distinctiveness. If you’re always trying to become someone else, you’re likely going to lose that. I don’t think that what we hope is a great run in college football is going to change us but we have to be deliberate in saying, ‘This is who we are.’” Living within the church’s rules Reese is something of a nontraditionalist himself. Before getting his “geek on,” and discovering a love for statistics, he fronted a punk rock band called Joe’s Wish. Reese jokes that the fact that it was a punk rock band only proves that he couldn’t sing. But it also means he appreciates the need to branch out, even if he finds solace in order. Before becoming a professor at BYU, he worked at Los Alamos National Laboratory, where he considered the readiness of the nation’s nuclear stockpile. As an academic, he studied everything from locating bowhead whale mating grounds to NASCAR. For a time, he even worked in sports analytics, helping fellow BYU alum Andy Reid when Reid was with the Eagles. All that to say the man understands numbers. Reese’s first day on the presidency job was on May 1, 2023; two months later, after 12 years as an independent, the Cougars joined the Big 12. In the three years since, the athletic departments revenues have skyrocketed from $47 million to $153 million. While the estimated $20 million spent on the football roster, according to The Athletic, pales in comparison to the some $50 million at Ohio State and Texas, it is not exactly chump change either. The statistician president understands the fiscal demands to remaining competitive, and the institutional benefits of being good at sports. But as university president, it is Reese’s job to make sure that, while everyone else around the country is playing with Monopoly money and accruing debt, BYU somehow minds its bottom line. The school is very clear about the church’s role in NIL. Quite simply, it has none. Yet the church also expects that both the institution and the athletic department remain debt-free. That’s the tug. There are other schools guided by religion – Notre Dame and Villanova are about to enjoy an audience with the Pope after playing in men’s and women’s basketball in Rome next month – but none is technically governed by its church. BYU’s board is chaired by the president of the church, who is also considered the church’s prophet, and members of the church’s Quorum of the Twelve Apostles are also BYU board members. The church’s expectation to live debt-free is not just an ask; it’s a requirement. “We absolutely have some reasonable guardrails in place,” Reese said. “Not assuming debt is tied to our sponsorship to the Church of Jesus Christ of the Latter-Day Saints. That is a principle they operate under. So, we might not have the shiniest buildings or maybe the doors squeak a bit on occasion, but those guardrails – we don’t take funds from the church, and we don’t assume debt as an athletic department – have served us well and they’re not going away.” The debate over doing more School officials will be the first to admit that not everyone agrees. BYU has some half a million living alumni. Most are content for the school to live within the means it has long existed under, but there are plenty who have enjoyed the taste of success and would like administrators to push a few more chips to the center. The school, after all, is not merely trying to be a viable independent; it is trying to be a Power 4 contender, with all the benefits that includes. “There are certainly some who feel like, if we’re going to be successful, we have to embrace what others are doing, and go with a more professional model,” says Keith Vorkink, BYU’s vice president of advancement. “But that’s not a tension we feel most of the time. You have to have some professional aspects. We’re not ignorant of that, but the key is do it in a way that aligns with our mission.” There is money in the Wasatch. Along with Smith, two other graduates – Mark Hancock (he’s No. 1,755 on Forbes) and Jason Murray – just agreed to a partnership between their alma mater and their company, PV3, to help fund NIL and facilities. Though the particulars weren’t disclosed, the school said it is the largest philanthropic donation to BYU athletics in school history. And then there is Jason McGowan, the mere megamillionaire owner of Crumbl Cookies, who could be a BYU savior. Last year, Penn State made a serious play for Sitake after canning James Franklin, offering well more than the $4 million BYU had been paying him. “Some people are not replaceable,” McGowan posted on X. “Sounds like it’s time for me to get off the sidelines and get to work.” A day later, Sitake signed an extension reportedly worth $9 million annually. But as critical as donor funding is, those who are providing the funds believe their wallets are not the path for sustainable BYU excellence. Instead, they look to the essence of the school – even with, or maybe because of, all of its idiosyncrasies – as its best value add. Smith sits on the NBA media committee and meets regularly with the people relocating to Utah amid a business boon. He studies the stuff not merely as a BYU fan, but as a businessman. “TV is driving the money in college sports,” he said. “What the Big Ten schools get annually through its TV contracts, you can’t get that through individual donors. The product has to be marketable. The schools ultimately that sit atop the rankings, the ones with name recognition, they’re going to be the most valuable.” The trick, then, is making your product marketable. Some 6.9 million church members live in the US, and while not all of them are football fans, plenty appreciate seeing the Cougars amplify their religion. “GameDay” enjoyed its third-best rating in show history on Saturday and at its peak, the Cougars game against Notre Dame drew 9.2 million viewers, the highest for a Big 12 team since 2022. “BYU draws,” Smith said. “That’s the part no one understands.” The vicious cycle of the current model, of course, is that to become marketable a team needs to get and retain good players, and to do that a school has to spend money, which cycles the whole thing back to the start. That means players have to be paid, and paid handsomely, which – in turn – runs against the very ethos of BYU. It feels like an impossible riddle to solve. BYU, though, thinks it has the solution. “You’ve got what seems like these competing interests,” Young says. “In the one hand you’re holding tight to the fact that we’re in the Big 12 and we have to be committed to the excellence of that. On the other hand, how do you build something that is so resonant to people that they would not actually just go take the last dollar? How do you get them stay for something more than the transaction, or build something that is not purely transactional? We call that the Kalani law of love.” Believing in the coach LaVell Edwards is something like the Joseph Smith of BYU football, both the founding father and the man who established the roadmap for the program’s success. Given the freedom to build something far away from the confines of Top 10 football, he engineered a pass-first offense during a time when most coaches still preferred the three-yards-and-a-cloud-of-dust approach. Beginning in 1972, the year Edwards was promoted to head coach, 11 consecutive running backs won the Heisman Trophy. Meanwhile in Provo, BYU gunslingers, beginning with Gary Sheide, were throwing for thousands of yards every season. A member of the church himself, Edwards leaned into, rather than obfuscated, its mission. He purposefully sought church members, crafting what would be termed the Polynesian pipeline by capitalizing on the heavy population of LDS members in places such as Tonga and Samoa. And after years at balking at holding scholarships for players who served their two-year missions, Edwards came around to understanding it was a way to get and keep his team older. Yet he also welcomed those who craved the school’s structure, if not its religion. Troublemaker Jim McMahon headed to BYU in no small part because his parents wanted him to find a little discipline. Twenty-six years after Edwards retired, one of his own is following his principles nearly to a T. Sitake came via the end around of the Polynesian pipeline. Born in Tonga, he was raised in Hawaii and schooled in Missouri. A fullback at BYU, he wound up team captain in his senior season. Young, who played for Edwards and has attended Sitake’s practices, is stunned at how similar they are. Sitake winds up practice with a prayer and insists that the defense and offense shake hands after going at one another all day. “We’re talking about love in football,” Young said. “It’s like saying, ‘There’s no crying in baseball.’ There’s no love in football, right? Well, yes there is. LaVell was all of that and Kalani is all of that.” Yet Sitake is entirely his own man. A bubble of happiness in a profession largely inhabited by the morose, he takes his job seriously, if not himself. He has, in various victory celebrations, done the cabbage patch and robot, and cracks jokes about both his affinity for ice cream and his fullback frame. His life has not been all jokes. Raised by a single father, he used to sit outside the BYU stadium and listen to games on the radio, the tickets too expensive for his family to afford. He spent one year at BYU before serving his mission in Oakland, California, returning to the Cougars as a redshirt before finally earning his way onto the field. Sitake also has a really hard job, no matter how much joy he brings to it. He is being asked to attract football players to a campus where they must operate under strict social guidelines with zero wiggle room for error. “It’s really hard what he’s doing,” Young said, “but he makes it look so easy.” Daring to be different Though 66 players on the current roster have served their mission, you cannot construct a roster entirely with LDS kids. Bringing non-church members to Provo requires a very different leap of faith. The school has worked hard to knock down the bogeyman perceptions. “We didn’t bring AJ here with the sole intent of converting him to our faith,” said Vorkink of No. 1 NBA draft pick AJ Dybantsa, who spent one season in Provo before leaving for the pros. “We have dozens of student-athletes who are not of our faith and feel like they belong in our community as much as anyone else.” Some have posited that the very thing that outsiders think makes BYU a hard sell – the lack of the normal college rites of passage – might be its best sales pitch. Smith, who spends hours signing and searching for professional basketball and hockey players, has noticed a slight shift in their mindsets. “It’s not the old frat boy college stereotype anymore,” he said. “Parents who want their kids to play at the next level, they want a place where you can keep the main thing the main thing. That’s what (BYU) offers.” But it has to be more than that. At the end of last season, BYU lost 13 players to the transfer portal; none were projected as starters for this season. “We are thriving in a Wild West situation,” Young said, “because Kalani is that special.” He added, “For some people, I know, this is ‘Oh my gosh! What is happening over there? It’s like magic.’ It’s like people think this will pass or something, but what we want people to understand is this is what we’ve been doing. It’s not new news. We’ve been hovering around 23,000 feet at base camp. Now we’re ready to summit Mount Everest.”

articles.title: Rebeca Andrade vuelve por todo lo alto y suma otro oro mundial en salto
articles.standfirst: Logra la tercera victoria en este aparato en un Mundial
articles.summary: Logra la tercera victoria en este aparato en un Mundial
articles.body: La brasileña Rebeca Andrade no decepcionó en su retorno a la gran competición internacional y se llevó el oro en salto en los Mundiales de Róterdam, tras deslumbrar con 14.466 puntos. La gimnasta brasileña reeditó sus títulos mundiales conquistados en 2021 y 2023, y sumó su tercera presea mundialista en la categoría de salto. La plata se la colgó la estadounidense Claire Pease (14.233 puntos) y Skye Blakely (14.166) se llevó el bronce, su tercera en este Campeonato del Mundo celebrado en la ciudad neerlandesa. La espectacular actuación de la campeona olímpica y mundial Andrade, que efectuó sus saltos bajo la mirada de su eterna rival, la estadounidense Simone Biles, puso en pie al público en las gradas y demostró por qué es una de las más grandes de la historia. La gimnasta sudamericana, que cumplió 27 años en mayo pasado, decidió hacer un parón en su carrera deportiva para recuperarse física y mentalmente de las exigencias del anterior ciclo olímpico, por lo que en su vuelta a la competición decidió competir en dos de los cuatro aparatos: la barra de equilibrios y el salto, en la que ha sumado una nueva medalla de oro a su extenso palmarés. Las canadienses Lia-Monica Fontaine y Elsabeth Black finalizaron en cuarta y quinta posición, mientras que la británica Abigail Martin terminó en último lugar. Por su parte, la mexicana Victoria Mata volvió a hacer historia para su país clasificándose para una final, en la que finalizó en sexta posición con 13.933 puntos.

articles.title: Gasperini: “A victory today would give us a huge boost.”
articles.summary: Gian Piero Gasperini spoke to DAZN shortly before kickoff for Napoli vs. Roma. The Giallorossi coach surprised everyone by launching Devyne Rensch on the win...
articles.body:
Gian Piero Gasperini spoke to DAZN shortly before kickoff for Napoli vs. Roma.

The Giallorossi coach surprised everyone by launching Devyne Rensch on the wing from the start, and behind Donyell Malen and Matias Soulé, he fielded Bryan Cristante, who had returned from injury.

What kind of match should we expect? "A high-level one. Lots of key players on the pitch, it's two of the best teams in the league."

How important is Cristante? "Important because we've often used the same players in his department. He's a top-level player, very versatile. He can play both against the deep end and allow someone else to push forward. We can have more tactical options with him."

Will Napoli-Roma shape the season? "Winning in Naples would be a step towards a special kind of awareness. From that perspective, it would undoubtedly be a great boost, but the season is still long."

articles.title: Ole Miss football’s key starting center good to go vs. Texas
articles.summary: Ole Miss football received an encouraging update on its offensive line ahead of Saturday night’s road matchup against Texas, with injuries affecting two star...
articles.body:
Ole Miss football received an encouraging update on its offensive line ahead of Saturday night's road matchup against Texas, with injuries affecting two starters entering the SEC clash.

Starting center Brycen Sanders and left tackle Terez Davis both suffered lower-body injuries during the Rebels' 31-3 victory over Missouri last week. Sanders returned to the game, while Davis remained on the sideline in uniform without reentering.

Both players appeared as questionable on the SEC's availability reports Wednesday and Thursday. Friday's update moved Sanders to probable, while Davis remained questionable.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The two linemen have started all six games this season for the No. 7 Rebels, who enter the matchup at 5-1 overall and 3-1 in SEC play.

On3's Pete Nakos reported Saturday on X, formerly Twitter, that sources expect Sanders to play against the Longhorns and anticipate a game-time decision on Davis' availability.

Sanders' expected availability would allow Patrick Kutas to remain at right guard after moving to center against Missouri. Kutas praised Sanders' handling of the offensive line's calls this week.

The senior center has appeared in 36 career games with 21 starts, including all 15 games at the position in 2025.

Davis' availability remains the outstanding question for the Rebels' offensive line. Connor Howes replaced him against Missouri, while true freshman Kane Mankins is listed as his backup on the depth chart.

Ole Miss has allowed an SEC-low 0.83 sacks per game while protecting quarterback Trinidad Chambliss. Texas has allowed just 106.3 rushing yards per game this season, presenting another challenge for the Rebels' offense in Austin.

The Longhorns will be without star edge rusher Colin Simmons, the nation's sack leader. The No. 19 Longhorns enter 4-2 overall and 1-2 in conference play.

Kickoff is scheduled for 7:30 p.m. ET/4:30 p.m. PT on ABC at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium in Austin, with Sanders expected to play and Davis' availability still unresolved.

articles.title: Gasperini: ‘Cristante gives Roma different variables, victory would show strength’
articles.summary: Gian Piero Gasperini notes Bryan Cristante gives Roma ‘different variables’ for the trip to Napoli, while a victory at the Stadio Maradona would ‘be another...
articles.body:
Gian Piero Gasperini notes Bryan Cristante gives Roma 'different variables' for the trip to Napoli, while a victory at the Stadio Maradona would 'be another show of strength.'

It kicks off at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona at 17.00 UK time (18.00 CEST).

NEWPORT, WALES – AUGUST 04: Gian Piero Gasperini, Head Coach of AS Roma, looks on before the pre-season friendly match between Newport County and AS Roma at Rodney Parade on August 04, 2026 in Newport, Wales. (Photo by Dan Istitene/Getty Images)

The Giallorossi saw their mood boosted by a midweek 4-0 victory over Slovan Bratislava in the Champions League, but it came at a price.

Lorenzo Pellegrini suffered a serious thigh tear and will be out for several months, joining Paulo Dybala, Manu Koné and Mile Svilar on the absentee list.

ROME, ITALY – OCTOBER 20: Gian Piero Gasperini, Manager of AS Roma, looks on during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 match between AS Roma and SK Slovan Bratislava at Stadio Olimpico on October 20, 2026 in Rome, Italy. (Photo by Paolo Bruno/Getty Images)

"It's a top level fixture with many important players, two of the best teams in the league, so it's a big game," Gasperini told DAZN Italia.

Cristante returns to the starting XI for the first time in over a month, but there are some doubts over the tactical set-up.

It remains to be seen who is in the more advanced role out of Cristante and Niccolò Pisilli today, in support of Donyell Malen and Matias Soulé, as it's possible Cristante is going to follow Napoli playmaker Kevin De Bruyne.

"Cristante is an important player because we often had to use the same figures in that role due to injuries, he also makes us a more versatile team, because we can play with two in midfield and push someone else forward. He can give us different variables during the match," confirmed Gasperini.

ROME, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 19: Manu Kone of AS Roma celebrates scoring his team's first goal with teammates during the Serie A match between AS Roma and FC Internazionale at Stadio Olimpico on September 19, 2026 in Rome, Italy. (Photo by Paolo Bruno/Getty Images)

Roma have not beaten Napoli since a 2-0 home result in December 2023, managing three draws and two losses.

Their most recent victory in Naples was a 4-2 thriller in March 2018, followed by four stalemates and as many defeats.

"It is early days in the season, but undoubtedly if we win away to Napoli, it would be another show of strength and a big push forward in terms of self-belief."

articles.title: Cowboys open practice window for key FA; defense inches closer to plan
articles.summary: It's been a revolving door in the Cowboys secondary over their first six games, but things are getting back to where the team wanted them in Week 1.
articles.body:
Dallas's defense continues to strengthen after early-season injuries have left the unit scrambling at times just to field 11 players over their first six contests.

The Cowboys opened the 21-day practice window for safety P.J. Locke on Friday , signaling that the eighth-year veteran is close to making his return from a torn plantar fascia suffered in September and four missed outings.

He's the latest Cowboys defender to hit the pathway back to the lineup; linebacker DeMarvion Overshown, cornerback Cobie Durant, and linebacker Marist Liufau all returned to practice this week as well.

Locke has played just 31 snaps for the Dallas defense in this, his first year wearing the star, but his renewed availability should put coordinator Christian Parker closer to his preferred gameday personnel as the Cowboys enter a stretch of their schedule that will likely decide their 2026 outlook.

The season opener saw the Cowboys start four defensive linemen, two linebackers on the middle level, and five defensive backs: rookie Caleb Downs as the nickel, two corners, and two safeties, Malik Hooker and Jalen Thompson. Week 2 in Washington used the same positional deployments, with Locke starting in place of Hooker, who had fractured a forearm versus the Giants.

By Week 3, Locke had gone down (after just three snaps against the Commanders), and Dallas mixed things up further to prepare for the Ravens' running attack of Lamar Jackson and Derrick Henry: an extra D-tackle up front and only one safety- Thompson- on the back end. Thompson did not make it through that game due to a hamstring injury. He's on IR but could start practicing again next week.

Hooker thankfully returned in Week 4, but the Cowboys had to supplement him at safety by borrowing Markquese Bell and Alijah Clark from special teams, shifting Downs off some of his nickel duties, and even promoting Juanyeh Thomas, who they had just signed to the practice squad four days prior.

That's been the Cowboys' safety platoon for the past three games. Of the team's listed safeties, Bell, who started the season as a backup on the depth chart, leads the group in defensive snaps, with nearly 50%.

Locke's return will be a welcome development indeed.

His official status for the Week 7 meeting with the Eagles, though, has not been revealed. It's likely the team will want to give him more of a ramp-up at practice before making him active, so an appearance Monday night seems like a long shot.

But he- and the Cowboys defense the way it was drawn up to start the once-promising season- is getting closer.

Todd is on X at @ToddBrock24f7 . Also, follow Cowboys Wire on Facebook to join in on the conversation with fellow fans!

articles.title: Swim and Dive: Northwestern’s men and women sweep Notre Dame
articles.summary: The ‘Cats took care of business in their final home meet of the season.
articles.body:
Northwestern swimming and diving got back on its feet on Friday, with its men's and women's teams both picking up resounding wins over Notre Dame.

The 'Cats returned home to the Norris Aquatic Center in hopes of a bounce-back performance, after dropping its first losses of the season against top-5 ranked Indiana and Texas in Bloomington, Indiana. And against the Fighting Irish, Northwestern found the reassuring wins it needed, as the NU men took down Notre Dame 186-114, while the NU women secured a 186-114 victory.

According to Swimcloud, Joshua Staples was the meet's high point on the men's side. However, the women's team did not place the meet's individual champion, with Notre Dame junior Hollie Widdows spoiling the party and besting NU first-year Flawia Kamzol for first place in the women's high point standings.

Results for the meet can be found on the Meet Mobile app or on Swimcloud's meet page for the event .

If interested in learning about how team and high point scoring works for dual-meets, please reference the section "Explanation of Dual-Meet Scoring System" at the bottom of the recap of the Northwestern-Miami (OH) dual-meet .

The No. 16-ranked Northwestern men's team made easy work of the Notre Dame men's team —a fast opponent who received 13 votes in the College Swimming and Diving Coaches Association of America's Division I preseason top 25 national rankings.

The 'Cats secured a 72-point victory over the Fighting Irish, winning seven of the meet's 12 individual swimming events, splitting the meet's two diving events and sweeping the meet's two relays.

An NU team of Stuart Seymour, Connor Schuster, Cade Duncan and Oli Kos took the crown in the 200-yard freestyle relay with a time of 1:17.97, while a Kos-Staples-Seymour-Duncan tandem touched first in the 400-yard medley relay with a time of 3:05.53.

Staples was the 'Cats' standout performer, taking home three individual event victories in the 100-yard breaststroke (52.67), 200-yard breaststroke (1:56.92) and 200-yard individual medley (1:46.43) in addition to his 51.53 100-yard breaststroke split in the 'Cats' gold medal-winning 400-yard medley relay. It was the Australian's first time swimming in the 200-yard breaststroke and 200-yard individual medley this season, while his 52.67 in the 100-yard breaststroke was good for a season-best time.

NU also claimed spots two and three on the high point podium. Seymour placed second after grabbing event wins in the 100-yard backstroke (45.32) and 100-yard butterfly (45.70) and Kos snagged third off victories in the 200-yard freestyle (1:36.26) and 200-yard backstroke (1:41.66). Meanwhile, the 'Cats' top diver of the meet was senior Adam Cohen, who won the three-meter diving competition and took second in one-meter diving.

Notre Dame's top performer was Shane Eckler, who took fourth with wins in the 50-yard freestyle (19.42) and 100-yard freestyle (42.79).

The Northwestern women won by a similar margin of 60 points against the Notre Dame women. Similar to the men, the NU women won seven of the meet's 12 individual swimming events, though off the flips and grace of senior Chloe Sharp, they swept the meet's one- and three-meter diving competitions.

The 'Cats went 1-1 in the meet's two relays, dropping the 400-yard medley relay by nearly 1.5 seconds to Notre Dame, who won with a time of 3:34.73, while a team of Kamzol, Aya Ferguson, Bri Deierlein and Amy Pan finished first in the 200-yard freestyle relay, posting a 1:30.41 that out-touched the Irish A-team's 1:30.43 by just two hundredths of a second.

Individually, Notre Dame's Widdows topped the women's high point standings after picking up wins in the 50-yard freestyle (22.55) and 100-yard freestyle (49.11).

However, outside of Widdows, NU claimed spots two through five on the leaderboard. For the third time this year in just as many competitions, first-year Kamzol was the 'Cats' highest finisher after she nabbed wins in the 100-yard backstroke (53.65) and 100-yard butterfly (52.30), swimming personal best times in each event. The Winetka senior Maggie Papanicholas took third in the standings after sweeping the breaststroke events, posting a 1:00.91 in the 100 and a 2:11.58 in the 200. And, per usual, junior distance specialist Zoe Noordman triumphed in the 500-yard freestyle (4:47.77) and 1650-yard freestyle (16:37.32), taking fourth, while Sharp took fifth off of her diving victories.

Northwestern's Friday wins over Notre Dame marked its last home meet of 2026 in the Norris Aquatic Center.

After three early-season competitions against Miami (OH), Texas/Indiana and Notre Dame, the 'Cats' fastest swimmers will head to their first peak meet of the season: the USA's first-ever Short Course World Championship Trials at FMC Natatorium from Oct. 28 to Oct. 31 in Westmont, Illinois. NU's Nordmann, Kamzol, Gerchik, Kos and Seymour are all technically seeded top five in an event in the meet's pre-scratch psych sheet , though their standings are inflated because they've all recently logged short course meters times at the Indiana/Texas SCM tri-meet, while most of the field is entered with converted long course meters times.

Following up Westmont, the 'Cats will head toward the sunrise to Durham, North Carolina, to face the Duke Blue Devils on Nov. 6 and Nov. 7.

articles.title: Saints announce practice squad moves for Week 7 Steelers matchup
articles.summary: Here are the standard weekly practice squad elevations for the Saints as the finalize preparations for their Paris game with the Pittsburgh Steelers.
articles.body:
On Saturday morning, the New Orleans Saints announced two practice squad elevations in advance of their Week 7 game against the Pittsburgh Steelers in Paris. The Saints are elevating wide receiver Cedric Tillman and offensive lineman Easton Kilty to the active roster against the Steelers. Both moves are standard weekly elevations, meaning each player will revert to the practice squad once the game is over.

Tillman, 26, played collegiately with the Tennessee Volunteers. Between 2018 and 2022, Tillman had 109 receptions for 1,622 yards and 17 scores, including 64 catches and 1,081 yards during the 2021 campaign. Tillman was a third round choice of the Cleveland Browns in the 2023 NFL Draft. He spent three seasons with the Browns and caught 71 balls for 833 yards with 5 touchdowns.

Son of former Denver Broncos wideout Cedric Tillman, Tillman was signed by New Orleans this offseason. He'd spent the season on the Saints practice squad before being elevated two weeks ago against Minnesota, playing just one offensive snap, and again last week against the New York Giants. Against the Giants, Tillman saw four offensive snaps and one on special teams. This is Tillman's third elevation, meaning the Saints are forced to decide whether to promote him to the active roster or release him outright after this week.

Kilty, 24, played collegiately at North Dakota State and Kansas State. He made the New Orleans practice squad as an undrafted rookie in 2025 but did not see any game action. Kilty was again kept on the Saints practice squad after 2026 training camp. He was elevated to the active roster for the Saints Week 5 game against the Vikings, getting two snaps on special teams but none on offense.

articles.title: Game Thread: TCU Football vs. West Virginia Mountaineers
articles.summary: Horned Frogs host Mountaineers in Big 12 battle
articles.body:
The TCU Horned Frogs (3-3; 1-2 Big 12) are back in action on Saturday morning in Amon G. Carter Stadium, hosting the West Virginia Mountaineers (4-3; 1-3 Big 12). It's a Homecoming celebration in Fort Worth as the Frogs return following a rivalry victory in Waco over the Baylor Bears. West Virginia is also coming off its first conference win of the season, outlasting Cincinnati with a 45-42 in Morgantown last week thanks to a 24-point 4th Quarter.

TCU enters the game as the Big 12's top defense, leading the league in points allowed, giving up just 12.2 points per game. The unit is powered by Koron Hayward, leading the Big 12 with 4.5 sacks. The Frogs offense has struggled however, ranking 15th in the league in points and dead last in the league in rushing.

West Virginia meanwhile is the top rushing team in the league, powered by one of the nation's top rushers, former Horned Frog Cam Cook who averages more per game individually (119 yards) than TCU does as a team (110 yards). Mountaineer QB Michael Hawkins has also been unleashed over the last few games, including a 464 yard, 3 TD performance last week against the Bearcats.

Which team will pick up its second Big 12 victory of the campaign and which will fall further into the league's basement? Join the conversation in the comment section below as we ride the game day rollercoaster together. Go Frogs!

articles.title: Why Joao Pedro Missed Chelsea vs Tottenham
articles.summary: As soon as the lineup dropped for Chelsea's London derby with Tottenham Hotspur, there was one very notable absence. Geovany Quenda was named to the starting...
articles.body:
As soon as the lineup dropped for Chelsea's London derby with Tottenham Hotspur, there was one very notable absence. Geovany Quenda was named to the starting eleven with it being clear that Joao Pedro was totally absent from the squad. The Brazilian has been in hot form since the start of the campaign, bagging five goals and three assists so far. His absence was a big worry for fans as his chemistry with Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers was a big part of Xabi Alonso's tactical ideology when attacking.

Joao Pedro Status Confirmed Following Tottenham Absence

Nizaar Kinsella was quick to cover the news, reporting that the player is out with an injury. The nature of the problem is currently unknown with the attacker "being assessed". Last week Malo Gusto missed out against Everton with a brief illness but there's no such luck this time for the Blues who are now dealing with an issue to their marquee striker.

Fans will be hoping it is only something minor, maybe a precaution over the problem that saw him get hurt earlier in the campaign. For now, all eyes will have to turn to the London derby without their prolific goalscorer.

The Brazilian striker has been dealing with injuries already in this term, he missed the loss to Brentford just before the international break. Any issue to him is likely to cause worry among the fans after his hot start to the season as well as the sale of Nicolas Jackson leaving the squad without a similar striking profile.

It was interesting that against the Lilywhites, Danny Welbeck wasn't given the nod to start. The veteran goalscorer is a decent option when physicality is needed but age does seem to hold him back when it comes to operating outside the box.

Blues fans will be hoping that this is just a temporary problem and that Pedro will be back firing and in fine form soon.

articles.title: Mississippi State QB Kamario Taylor receives encouraging injury update before Oklahoma game
articles.summary: Mississippi State was shut out 31-0 at LSU last Saturday while Kamario Taylor watched from the sideline with a boot on his right foot. The Bulldogs finished...
articles.body:
Mississippi State was shut out 31-0 at LSU last Saturday while Kamario Taylor watched from the sideline with a boot on his right foot. The Bulldogs finished with 291 total yards and 121 passing yards behind freshman Parker "Billy" Puckett, who was making his first career start.

"He didn't wake up yesterday morning and was healed," Mississippi State coach Jeff Lebby said Monday .

ESPN's Pete Thamel reported on Friday that Taylor is expected to dress and attempt to play when the Bulldogs host Oklahoma at 3:30 p.m. ET on SEC Network. Thamel also reported that Taylor took significantly more snaps in practice this week. Mississippi State has not publicly detailed the injury, which Thamel described as a foot and toe issue.

How different is Mississippi State's offense without Taylor?

Taylor has thrown for 1,450 yards with 17 touchdowns and four interceptions in five games, completing 66.2% of his passes. Against LSU, Puckett went 16 of 26 for 121 yards with an interception and was sacked three times. Lebby said after the game that Taylor had worked hard to get back but was not quite ready to play.

Oklahoma's defense allows 260.7 yards per game, fifth-fewest in the country, and it arrives in Starkville for the programs' first-ever meeting with little help from its own offense. The Sooners rank last in the SEC in total offense at roughly 311 yards per game . John Mateer threw three interceptions in last week's 21-13 home loss to Kentucky, giving him seven in six games, and Oklahoma sits at minus-8 in turnover margin.

Oklahoma is 3-3 and 1-2 in the SEC. Mississippi State is 4-2 and 2-2, and it entered the LSU game ranked No. 16 before the shutout handed it a second straight loss . In a game between a strong defense and an offense that keeps giving the ball away, the quarterback with the cleaner turnover record holds an obvious edge, and that quarterback is Taylor, with four interceptions in five games against Mateer's seven in six. Puckett's lone start produced no points against LSU.

Taylor carried a questionable tag on this week's first SEC availability report, the same designation he held early in LSU week. That week, he was downgraded to doubtful the night before the game and ruled out 90 minutes before kickoff.

"It's going to be day-to-day. He's got a lot of work to do, but we'll see where we end up," Lebby said in the same Monday news conference.

articles.title: Tim Tebow’s Arch Manning defense comes with stats that may concern Texas fans
articles.summary: Florida beat Texas 27-24 in Austin on Oct. 17, sealing it with an Arch Manning fumble in the final two minutes and handing the Longhorns a second straight lo...
articles.body:
Florida beat Texas 27-24 in Austin on Oct. 17, sealing it with an Arch Manning fumble in the final two minutes and handing the Longhorns a second straight loss to an unranked opponent. On Friday, the Gators' most famous quarterback went on SportsCenter to defend the Texas quarterback his old school had just beaten.

Tim Tebow agreed that Manning has to play better. He also argued that the quarterback is taking blame that belongs to other people, and he came with numbers.

"It's easy to jump on the bandwagon of criticizing the young man. I just don't believe it's fair, I don't believe it's accurate. Yes, I think Arch needs to improve, I think he will improve, and he has to make more plays," Tebow said.

"But equally as important, he's got to get more help. His offensive line has to improve. Receivers, although they're really talented, they also have to improve when they're getting 1-on-1. And here's some stats I want to share with you. The last three weeks the pressure rate for the Texas offense has been 137th in the FBS, the sack rate 135th in the FBS, yards before contact for their rushers, 0.5, 127th in the FBS. So it's really easy to say it's all on Arch. It's just not true," he continued.

Against Florida, Texas ran for 99 yards, gave up five sacks and was stopped on both a fourth-and-1 and a fourth-and-2. The second stop came near midfield with Texas trailing 20-17 in the fourth quarter, and Florida turned it into a touchdown.

A week earlier against Oklahoma, Manning threw a pick-six and then a second fourth-quarter interception that set up the Sooners' winning field goal. The Austin American-Statesman's film review showed Oklahoma defensive back Michael Boganowski coming through the line untouched on that second pick.

On the play that ended the Florida game, the same review found receiver Emmett Mosley V open on an out route before the Gators' blitz got home. Manning held the ball, took the sack and lost the fumble.

A line ranked 137th in pressure rate over a three-week stretch shortens every dropback, and in back-to-back fourth quarters Manning has been forced to decide faster than he has shown he can. That snap against Florida belongs to him. The conditions that produced it belong to the men in front of him, which is why Tebow's split of the blame holds up better than the version that puts all of it on the quarterback.

Could Texas pull Manning if Ole Miss jumps out early?

"I would use the word edgy, and I like it. He's edgy right now. And I think that somebody texted me today that we lost the 'Aw Shucks' kid, and we created something else," Steve Sarkisian told reporters on Thursday .

After the Florida loss, Sarkisian said "everything" about the offense would be evaluated, and backup KJ Lacey was in line for more first-team reps in practice this week. Texas is 4-2 and ranked No. 19, and another loss could knock the Longhorns out of playoff contention entirely with No. 7 Ole Miss visiting Austin on Saturday night.

"It just depends, every game's different. So I think Arch has had a good week of work, he's prepared himself well. But like the team, we need to play well, so we'll go from there," Sarkisian said when asked if Manning could come out of a game for reasons other than a blowout.

articles.title: Utah HC Morgan Scalley sends clear message about his future with the Utes
articles.summary: Morgan Scalley is scheduled to join College GameDay live from Presidents Circle on Saturday morning, the third time in four seasons ESPN’s pregame show has s...
articles.body:
Morgan Scalley is scheduled to join College GameDay live from Presidents Circle on Saturday morning, the third time in four seasons ESPN's pregame show has set up on Utah's campus. The first visit came in 2004, when Scalley was a senior safety on an unbeaten Utes team.

He now coaches a 6-0 team ranked No. 10, one of five FBS programs still without a loss, with No. 14 Houston coming to Rice-Eccles Stadium for a 10:15 p.m. ET kickoff.

That backdrop brought a story from March back up on Friday.

That month, Scalley and his wife, Liz, pledged $2 million to the Utah football program , a gift athletic director Mark Harlan announced before Scalley had coached a regular-season game as head coach.

"My love for this place includes a vision of where we can go and what we can achieve, and it will require an increased effort from everyone who shares in that vision. Liz and I simply wanted to do something for this amazing place that shows our faith in and commitment to the future of this incredible University, and how excited we are for what's to come," Scalley said in the school's announcement .

"Utah's done a ton for me and my family. My wife went here. My entire family went to the University of Utah. There's a lot the Utah family has given us," Scalley said on The Pat McAfee Show, per On3 .

"This is not a Morgan Scalley thing. I said that early on. It's about Utah football. It's about the University of Utah. When I'm gone, again, it'll still be Utah. We wanted to give back and help this community understand that we're in this together. I'm not going anywhere unless they kick me out of here," he added.

How much of his own salary did Scalley give back?

Scalley's five-year, $27 million contract pays a base salary of $3.6 million this season , with $150,000 raises in each year after. The $2 million pledge is more than half of that first-year base. Even with the $1 million promotional payment and the $500,000 from Under Armour included in each year of the deal, the gift equals roughly 39% of what the contract pays him in its first year before incentives.

Kyle Whittingham coached Utah for 21 seasons before taking the Michigan job, about two weeks after Scalley signed his deal in December. Scalley, a Salt Lake City native, has coached nowhere else. He started as an administrative assistant with the Utes in 2006 and spent the last 10 of his 18 seasons as an assistant running the defense. Coming from a coach whose entire career has run through one program, "I'm not going anywhere" sounds like a plain statement of fact.

If Scalley leaves for another job before the deal expires, he owes Utah 75% of his base salary and other contract payments for each remaining year, the same share the school would owe him if it fired him without cause.
